title: Digital transformation, supply chain integration, and supply chain performance: A bibliometric analysis of Scopus research trends (2016–2025)
summary: This study maps the development of research on the relationship between digital transformation, supply chain integration, and supply chain performance. It responds to the need for a focused bibliometric account of how digital technologies are positioned within supply chain management research beyond broad reviews of the field. A Scopus export dated 3 June 2026 was analysed, comprising 188 English-language records published between 2016 and 2025, including 174 articles and 14 reviews. Records were identified through a structured search strategy and analysed using descriptive bibliometric techniques, citation analysis, author productivity analysis, country analysis, and keyword normalisation. The results show substantial growth in publication activity, rising from 1 record in 2016 to 74 records in 2025. However, the most recent publication year should be interpreted with caution because database coverage remains sensitive to indexing and update cycles. The corpus accumulated 8562 Scopus citations, with a mean of 45.5 citations per record and a median of 19.5 citations per record. Sustainability (Switzerland), International Journal of Production Economics, Journal of Enterprise Information Management, Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review, and Supply Chain Management emerged as the most visible publication outlets. Normalised keyword patterns indicate that supply chain integration, supply chain performance, digital transformation, supply chain resilience, blockchain, collaboration, Industry 4.0, visibility and the Internet of Things constitute the dominant vocabulary of the field. The study contributes by showing that contemporary scholarship increasingly conceptualises supply chain performance as dependent on digitally enabled integration, visibility, collaboration, and organisational coordination capabilities.

title: THE EFFECT OF ACCOUNTING CONSERVATISM AND CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY (CSR) DISCLOSURE ON EARNINGS MANAGEMENT: EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE FROM CONSUMER GOODS INDUSTRY COMPANIES LISTED ON THE DURING 2022–2025
summary: This study examines the effects of accounting conservatism and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) disclosure on earnings management in consumer goods industry companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022–2025 period. Earnings management remains a major concern because it can reduce the reliability of financial reporting and create information asymmetry between management and stakeholders. This study employed a quantitative approach with a causal explanatory design using panel data regression analysis. The sample consisted of 44 consumer goods companies selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 176 firm-year observations. Earnings management was measured using discretionary accruals based on the Modified Jones Model, accounting conservatism was measured using the Conservative Accruals (CONACC) model, and CSR disclosure was measured using the Corporate Social Responsibility Disclosure Index (CSRDI). The results indicate that accounting conservatism has a positive and significant effect on earnings management, while CSR disclosure has a negative and significant effect on earnings management. Furthermore, accounting conservatism and CSR disclosure simultaneously have a significant effect on earnings management. These findings suggest that CSR disclosure contributes to reducing opportunistic reporting behavior, whereas accounting conservatism may provide managerial discretion that influences reported earnings.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, AND GOVERNANCE (ESG) PERFORMANCE AND EARNINGS MANAGEMENT: THE ROLE OF AUDIT QUALITY
summary: Grounded in Agency and Stakeholder theories, this research explores the influence of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance on earnings management, while also assessing whether audit quality serves as a moderating factor. The magnitude of earnings manipulation is evaluated using discretionary accruals. By applying a purposive sampling technique, the study analyzes 238 firm-year observations from non-financial corporations registered on the Indonesia Stock Exchange between 2020 and 2024. The data is processed utilizing Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The empirical outcomes reveal that organizations demonstrating superior ESG achievements are less likely to engage in earnings management. Conversely, audit quality, measured by the presence of a Big Four auditor, fails to show a significant moderating effect in reinforcing the linkage between ESG practices and reduced earnings manipulation. title: Aligning Corporate Governance with ILO Labor Standards: Challenges and Opportunities for Multinational Enterprises
summary: Multinational enterprises increasingly recognize the importance of aligning corporate governance frameworks with International Labor Organization requirements, but scholarship on this intersection remains limited. This paper addresses that gap by synthesizing evidence that improved governance mechanisms notably enhance labor compliance throughout international operations. The International Labor Organization establishes foundational requirements for respectable work—encompassing freedom of association, collective bargaining, non-discrimination, and workplace safety—that multinational firms have to operationalize through corporate decision-making systems and supply chain governance. Contemporary multinational businesses navigate competing pressures from regulators, shareholders, and civil society while managing labor-related human rights obligations across jurisdictions. Stakeholder-centric governance frameworks provide promising pathways for forums to institutionalize labor issues within operational workflows. Evidence demonstrates that active board oversight, strong due diligence mechanisms, and independent verification structures significantly improve compliance outcomes compared to voluntary codes alone. Leading multinationals in electronics, clothing, and extractive industries have correctly incorporated ILO-aligned measures into center governance systems, promoting both compliance and stakeholder engagement. However, effective implementation remains constrained by functional governance potential gaps in host nations and chronic deficiencies in corporate disclosure verification. This paper argues that integrating ILO standards into company governance constitutes both a strategic imperative for operational resilience and a mechanism for advancing sustainable development. Recommendations emphasize bolstered board duty, comprehensive supply chain due diligence, and unbiased outside verification regimes.

title: Examining the Impact of Corporate Information Communication Technology Resources on the Corporate Social Responsibility Performance of Tokyo‐Listed Firms
summary: ABSTRACT Corporate Information Communication Technology (ICT) assets play a vital role in improving corporate social responsibility (CSR) outcomes. They help with data management, increase transparency, and support effective communication with stakeholders. These abilities allow companies to better monitor, record, and implement socially and environmentally responsible actions. This research, based on the Resource‐Based View, investigates how corporate ICT assets influence CSR performance. It also examines whether firm size and innovation orientation influence this relationship. The study employed specific inclusion and exclusion criteria and utilized a purposive sampling method to select suitable firms. Data were collected from 483 non‐financial corporations of Tokyo‐listed firms between 2008 and 2024. Researchers gathered this information from the Bloomberg database. To confirm the reliability and strength of the findings, advanced second‐generation estimation methods were used. These included the Augmented Mean Group (AMG), the Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCEMG), and the two‐step Generalized Method of Moments (GMM). The findings indicate that investments in ICT, the intensity of ICT use, and ICT‐related research and development, as indicators of corporate ICT resources, have a positive impact on CSR performance. Additionally, interactions between ICT investment, firm size, and innovation orientation had significant positive effects on CSR outcomes. This highlights the need for corporate leaders to focus on building ICT infrastructure as part of their CSR and sustainability strategies, especially regarding CSR reporting and stakeholder engagement. The study also emphasizes the importance of policymakers in promoting digital transformation to enhance responsible corporate governance.

title: Peer Accounting Comparability and Focal Firms’ Earnings Management: A Perspective of Accounting Discretion
summary: This study investigates how firms manage earnings through accounting discretion when industry peers produce more comparable accounting information. Utilizing data from Chinese A‐share listed firms, we find that peer accounting comparability inhibits focal firms’ accruals‐based earnings management. We identify two possible mechanisms underlying this phenomenon. First, peer accounting comparability helps to establish generally accepted accounting practices that induce focal firms to align. Second, peer accounting comparability contributes to mitigating outsiders’ information asymmetry, thus improving external monitoring. Cross‐sectional analysis indicates that the effect of peer accounting comparability holds across varying levels of focal firms’ internal and external governance mechanisms. Furthermore, we find that manipulating accruals when peer accounting comparability is high causes lower cumulative abnormal returns during the earnings announcement window and a higher cost of equity. Finally, we show that when focal firms cannot manage earnings through accounting discretion because of high peer accounting comparability, they turn to real earnings management.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN AUDITING AND ACCOUNTING: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is addressed in accounting and auditing research in relation to financial reporting, assurance services, fraud detection, risk management, and professional decision-making processes. This study combines data source-sensitive bibliometric profiling with VOSviewer-based text network analysis. Records, citations, annual citations, author-focused metrics, and the Age-Weighted Citation Rate accessed via Publish or Perish from Google Scholar, CrossRef, OpenAlex, Scopus, and Semantic Scholar data sources were compared. The findings indicate that bibliometric indicators vary depending on the data source, and that Scopus text networks offer a narrower, source-specific view of the core themes represented in the accessed records.

title: PENGARUH CORPORATE GOVERNANCE TERHADAP TAX AVOIDANCE
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of corporate governance on tax avoidance in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2022–2024 period. The corporate governance variables analyzed in this study include board independence, board gender diversity, board size, audit quality, and CEO narcissism, as well as financial characteristic variables, namely profitability and leverage. Tax avoidance is measured using the effective tax rate (ETR). This study employs a quantitative approach with a causal research design. The research sample was selected using a purposive sampling method, and secondary data were obtained from companies’ annual reports and financial statements. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, data quality tests, classical assumption tests, and hypothesis testing through multiple linear regression analysis. The results indicate that board independence, board gender diversity, board size, and audit quality do not have a significant effect on tax avoidance. Furthermore, CEO narcissism and leverage have a positive and significant effect on tax avoidance. Meanwhile, profitability has a negative and significant effect on tax avoidance.

title: System, Method, and Cryptographic Enclave for Sub-8 Millisecond Pre-Flight Statutory Sanctions Gating, Mathematical Solvency Auditing, and Hardware-Isolated Key Attestation with Zero-Wire Leakage in Decentralized Multi-Rail Clearing Networks

Abstract A hardware-isolated cryptographic enclave system, edge execution method, and communication protocol for enforcing pre-flight statutory compliance, anti-money laundering (AML) sanctions screening, and zero-leakage mathematical solvency within an edge execution environment prior to transaction broadcast across public distributed ledgers. An out-of-order 256-bit sliding window nonce bitmap mapped across 256 concurrent execution lanes via SHA3-256 rendezvous hashing, preventing mempool head-of-line blocking; and5. An atomic dual-signature attestation coupling a classical 64-byte Ed25519 signature with a 67-chain Winternitz One-Time Signature (WOTS+, RFC 8391) post-quantum checkpoint leaf, root-attested within locked memory (`mlock`) to permanently bar host operating system page extraction. title: Pengaruh Financial Distress dan Leverage terhadap Earnings Management dengan ESG Disclosure sebagai Variabel Moderasi
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji pengaruh financial distress dan leverage terhadap manajemen laba serta menganalisis peran moderasi pengungkapan Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG). Penelitian dilakukan pada perusahaan sektor Consumer Non-Cyclicals yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) selama periode 2019–2024. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan teknik purposive sampling dan memperoleh 262 observasi firm-year dari 105 perusahaan yang memenuhi kriteria penelitian. Manajemen laba diukur menggunakan discretionary accruals berdasarkan Modified Jones Model, financial distress diukur menggunakan Altman Z-Score, leverage diproksikan dengan Debt to Equity Ratio (DER), sedangkan pengungkapan ESG diukur menggunakan ESG Disclosure Index (ESGDI). Data dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda dan Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) dengan bantuan SPSS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa financial distress tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap manajemen laba, dan leverage juga tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap manajemen laba. Selain itu, pengungkapan ESG tidak terbukti memoderasi hubungan antara financial distress dan manajemen laba. Namun, pengungkapan ESG terbukti memoderasi secara signifikan hubungan antara leverage dan manajemen laba, yang menunjukkan bahwa pengungkapan ESG dapat mengubah kekuatan pengaruh leverage terhadap manajemen laba. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa tekanan keuangan tidak selalu mendorong perusahaan untuk melakukan manajemen laba, sedangkan pengungkapan ESG berperan dalam membentuk perilaku manajerial, khususnya pada kondisi perusahaan dengan tingkat leverage yang tinggi.

title: Green Supply Chain Finance and Systemic Risks in the Global South's Green Transition: An Approach Towards SDG 9
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how green supply chain finance relates to systemic risks, including competitiveness risk, financial instability risk, and green transition‐related geopolitical exposure, across 15 Global South economies from 2014 to 2024. Extending prior firm‐level research, this study conceptualizes green supply chain finance as a macro‐level financial mechanism linking industrial transformation to systemic stability. A composite index of green supply chain finance is constructed using green financing and policy indicators, and panel fixed‐effects models are complemented by heteroskedasticity‐based instrumental variable estimation to address endogeneity. The results show that green supply chain finance is consistently associated with lower competitiveness risks and exhibits weaker but generally negative associations with financial instability and transition‐related external risks. Overall, the findings extend the green finance literature by providing cross‐country evidence on the relationship between green supply chain finance and systemic resilience, with implications for sustainable industrial development and the broader objectives of Sustainable Development Goal 9.

title: Insights Into the Roles of the Corporate Governance Mechanism in Sustainability Assurance Practices
summary: ABSTRACT Our study explores the roles of corporate governance mechanisms in sustainability assurance practices in China through 40 semi‐structured interviews with sustainability reporting preparers and assurance providers. Guided by framing theory, the findings unveil distinct frames of the two groups perceiving governance of sustainability assurance. Six influential governance mechanisms emerge, including boards of directors, audit committees, internal auditors, the Communist Party Committee, governing bodies and external assurance providers. Three insights are identified from the interviewees' storylines: (1) the Chinese central government and its authority departments dominate the sustainability assurance legitimacy process, (2) in the absence of comprehensive assurance standards, legitimacy needs to be maintained to constrain managerial opportunism and (3) organisational and regional cultural factors shape report preparers' and assurance providers' perceptions of sustainability activities. Our study extends the application of framing theory by providing preliminary evidence of legitimised corporate governance roles in an emerging economy context.

title: PENGARUH CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, FINANCIAL RATIO, AND OTHER FACTORS TERHADAP FIRM VALUE
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of profitability, firm size, total asset growth, liquidity, leverage, total asset turnover, and audit committee structure on firm value. The population consists of manufacturing sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2020–2024 period, with 79 firms selected as samples using purposive sampling. Hypothesis testing was conducted using multiple linear regression analysis. The results show that profitability has a positive effect on firm value, as a higher ability to generate profits attracts investor interest. Total asset growth has a negative effect on firm value, indicating that asset growth without improvements in profitability and business sustainability is less attractive to investors. Leverage has a positive effect on firm value, reflecting the company’s ability to manage debt optimally. Meanwhile, total asset turnover has a negative effect on firm value, as high asset turnover does not represent an overall improvement in company performance. Firm size, liquidity, and audit committee structure have no effect on firm value.

title: Debt covenant violations and corporate financing and investment decisions: A financial statement decomposition approach
summary: This study examines how debt covenant violations are associated with subsequent corporate financing and investment behavior. We organize financing outcomes using an accounting-based decomposition of free cash flow and apply a common regression specification to estimate how the conditional association with covenant violations is distributed across cash accumulation, net equity distributions, and net debt distributions. Using U.S. public firms with reported covenant violations over 1996–2019, we find that violations are followed by higher cash accumulation and greater net repayments to debt holders, while net equity distributions show little systematic change. The resulting free-cash-flow association is accounted for primarily by debt-side adjustment and, to a lesser extent, cash accumulation. On the investment side, violations are followed by reductions in capital expenditures and acquisitions, but we find no robust evidence of reductions in research and development or operating lease expenses. Subperiod tests show that higher debt repayment and lower capital expenditures and acquisitions persist across changing lending environments, although the aggregate free-cash-flow association weakens in the most recent period. Overall, the evidence indicates selective post-violation conservatism in financing and investment policies, which may reflect the joint adjustment of creditors and managers as well as underlying changes in firms’ financial condition.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in Financial Services: Emerging Business Models, Opportunities and Challenges
summary: ABSTRACT The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), cloud computing, big data analytics, blockchain and digital payment technologies is transforming the structure and functioning of modern commerce. The financial services sector is one of the most technology-intensive sectors, where digital transformation has changed traditional banking, payment systems, lending, investment management, insurance and customer relationship management. Artificial Intelligence has emerged as a particularly important technology because of its ability to analyse large volumes of structured and unstructured data, identify patterns, automate decisions and provide personalised services.This chapter examines the role of Artificial Intelligence in transforming financial services and creating emerging business models. It discusses major applications of AI in banking and finance, including fraud detection, credit assessment, customer service, personalised financial products, risk management, regulatory compliance, investment management and digital payments. The chapter also examines emerging models such as AI-powered banking, embedded finance, Banking-as-a-Service, FinTech platforms, intelligent digital lending and AI-enabled financial ecosystems. At the same time, the adoption of AI introduces challenges related to data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, model risk, technological dependency and regulatory compliance. The chapter proposes a responsible AI adoption framework based on governance, data quality, transparency, human oversight, cybersecurity and continuous monitoring. The discussion is particularly relevant to emerging markets such as India, where digital public infrastructure and FinTech innovation are rapidly changing the financial ecosystem.

title: Cross-industry Technological Information Spillovers through Analyst Networks
summary: Do equity analysts transmit technological information across industries? I show that, through within-brokerage networks, analysts acquire technological knowledge from firms in other industries and apply it to the firms they cover. I measure these spillovers using technological connectedness (TC), based on patent-distribution similarity between a focal firm and firms covered by colleagues in other industries. Using brokerage M&As as quasi-exogenous shocks to analyst networks, I show that higher-TC analysts issue more accurate earnings forecasts. At the firm level, high-TC analysts improve innovation quality by curbing low-impact patenting. Coverage by high-TC analysts also attenuates technology momentum in stock returns.

title: Regulatory Extraterritoriality in EU ESG Governance
summary: This article explores how the European Union’s Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) regulatory framework is creating de facto global standards that reach well beyond Europe’s borders. It argues that EU ESG rules represent a significant evolution of the classic ‘Brussels Effect’, extending the EU’s regulatory influence from traditional product standards to the way companies govern themselves, organize their operations, and manage their global value chains. Through landmark instruments the EU is actively shaping corporate behaviour around the world. The article identifies four key mechanisms driving this global diffusion: market access pressure, supply chain governance, financial market alignment, and normative legitimacy. In doing so, it conceptualizes this phenomenon as a new form of conduct-based extraterritoriality, in which EU rules increasingly influence not only what companies produce, but how they operate internally and across borders. At the same time, the article acknowledges important limitations, including growing regulatory fragmentation, high compliance costs (particularly for firms in developing countries), and rising geopolitical contestation. Ultimately, EU ESG regulation emerges as a powerful yet increasingly contested force in the transformation of global governance.

title: AI-Driven Self-Healing Supply Chains and the Future of Logistics Automation
summary: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) enables self-healing capabilities in global supply chains and reshapes logistics automation. Employing a qualitative multi-case study design, data were collected through 42 semi-structured interviews across six multinational organisations in manufacturing, retail, and third-party logistics. Thematic analysis yielded four themes: AI-enabled disruption sensing; autonomous reconfiguration mechanisms; human-AI collaboration and workforce transformation; and ethical and governance considerations. Findings demonstrate that self-healing capability emerges from the dynamic interplay between AI infrastructure, adaptive organisational routines, and human agency - not from technology alone. Organisations embedding AI within a dynamic capabilities’ framework achieve measurable reductions in disruption recovery time and operational costs. A grounded theoretical model of AI-driven supply chain self-healing is proposed, integrating dynamic capabilities theory and complex adaptive systems theory. Practical implications for supply chain leaders and directions for future mixed-methods research are discussed.

title: Labor Mobility in the Context of Globalization and the Digital Economy
summary: The article analyzes the transformation of labor mobility under the impact of the digital economy. The study aims to substantiate that digitalization replaces the physical relocation of workers with their virtual integration into employers' processes, and to assess whether the current level of digitalization in Russia is sufficient for full-scale labor mobility by 2028. The empirical basis comprises data from the statistical compendium "Digital Economy Indicators: 2026" (HSE University / Rosstat). The findings reveal that remote and platform-based employment cover 1.7% and 3.8% of the workforce respectively, with the highest intensity of remote work recorded in the IT industry (23.4%). Three systemic barriers are identified: a skills deficit (only 10.6% of the population possess basic or higher digital skills, while 75.4% lack information security competencies), infrastructural constraints (corporate VPN usage stands at merely 35.8% of organizations), and scale limitations (the ICT sector contributes 4.0% to GVA, equivalent to 3.9% of GDP, versus 7–9% in leading countries). The theoretical contribution lies in conceptualizing two divergent trajectories of digital mobility: genuine virtual integration and algorithmically mediated local employment. The study concludes that the current level of digitalization is insufficient for systemic labor market virtualization by 2028, a qualitative shift is realistically achievable no earlier than 2030–2032.

title: Digital Transformation of Indian Commerce and the Changing World of Work: A Conceptual Review of Business, Employment and Workforce Capability
summary: This conceptual review examines how digital transformation is reshaping Indian commerce and the world of work that sustains it. Adopting an integrative literature review design, the study synthesises 30 scholarly and institutional sources, comprising foundational theory on technology and organisations, recent evidence on automation and artificial intelligence, and India-focused research and official reports on digitalisation, employment, informality and leadership, through thematic analysis. Four themes emerge: the digitalisation of commercial activity, the recomposition of employment, the centrality of workforce capability and leadership, and the risk of a widening divide between the organised economy and traditional and unorganised sectors. Official estimates place India's digital economy at 11.74% of national income in 2022-23, with a projected share of nearly one-fifth by 2029-30, which underlines the scale of the shift. The synthesis indicates that the employment effects of digitalisation are compositional and not uniformly negative, that returns to digital investment depend on complementary human and organisational capabilities, and that the informal workforce, including handloom producers, construction labour and migrant workers, remains largely outside the digital dividend. The paper integrates these insights into a Digital Commerce–Work–Capability framework and advances five research propositions for empirical testing. It offers practical guidance for business managers, educational institutions and policymakers seeking inclusive digital growth.

title: GENDER DIVERSITY AND FINANCIAL REPORTING QUALITY OF LISTED NON- FINANCIAL FIRMS IN NIGERIA: THE MODERATING ROLE OF DIGITAL GOVERNANCE
summary: Abstract This study examines the effect of gender diversity on financial reporting quality of listed non-financial firms in Nigeria, and the moderating role of digital governance. Specifically, it tests the influence of female directors’ educational qualifications and IT expertise on absolute discretionary accruals, and whether digital governance alters these relationships. Motivated by persistent concerns over earnings management and the increasing role of technology in corporate oversight, the study uses ex post facto design. Secondary data were obtained from the annual reports of 38 firms on the Nigerian Exchange Group for 2016–2025. Financial reporting quality was measured with absolute discretionary accruals. Descriptive statistics, correlation, and panel regression with robust standard errors were applied. Results show that female directors’ education has a positive but insignificant effect on reporting quality. Female IT expertise has a positive and significant effect on discretionary accruals, suggesting lower reporting quality. However, digital governance significantly moderates the IT expertise–reporting quality link, weakening the adverse effect. The moderation for education is not significant. The study concludes that the impact of gender diversity is attribute-specific and contingent on digital governance. It recommends that firms strengthen digital governance and integrate female IT directors into financial oversight to improve reporting quality. JEL Classification: G34, M41, G32, O55

Descriptive statistics, correlation, and panel regression with robust standard errors were applied. Results show that female directors’ education has a positive but insignificant effect on reporting quality. Female IT expertise has a positive and significant effect on discretionary accruals, suggesting lower reporting quality. However, digital governance significantly moderates the IT expertise–reporting quality link, weakening the adverse effect. The moderation for education is not significant. The study concludes that the impact of gender diversity is attribute-specific and contingent on digital governance. It recommends that firms strengthen digital governance and integrate female IT directors into financial oversight to improve reporting quality. JEL Classification: G34, M41, G32, O55

title: A Framework for Supplier Management Based on Environmental, Social, and Governance Criteria for Small and Medium‐Sized Enterprises
summary: ABSTRACT Corporate sustainability, grounded in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) dimensions, has become a strategic imperative for firms seeking competitiveness and resilience. In supply chain management, supplier selection is a key mechanism for translating ESG principles into practice. However, small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly in emerging economies, face resource constraints that hinder the adoption of complex ESG frameworks. Thus, this study proposes an ESG‐based supplier management framework tailored to SMEs in emerging economies. A systematic literature review and an expert survey were used to identify and assess ESG criteria for supplier management. The Fuzzy Delphi Method and Multiattribute Utility Theory were applied to refine and prioritize criteria based on relevance and applicability. Results highlight the central role of social criteria, with governance acting as an enabling pillar and environmental practices playing a complementary role. The framework provides a structured and decision‐support tool for ESG integration in SME supply chains.

title: Circularity beyond recycling: toward a regenerative supply chain philosophy a conceptual framework
summary: This conceptual paper on the shortcomings of the circular economy model and proposes an approach towards regenerative supply chains where there is an inherent philosophy of restoring the ecosystems in design, rather than addressing end-of-life recovery when recycling alone cannot reduce the environmental footprint. This conceptual framework is developed by conducting an iterative process of thematic analysis of the ecological economics, cradle-to-cradle approach, and complex adaptive system theories through the review of 39 peer-reviewed articles. This paper presents a conceptual and theoretical framework and not an empirical study. Existing circular economy concepts continue the practice of extraction and ignore the problems of rebound effects. The idea of regenerative supply chain is introduced to improve natural and socio-economic ecosystems using the combination of ecosystem services, digitization, and policymaking. Originality/Value: This paper offers a new concept of regenerative supply chain in which regeneration is viewed as a continuous, spiral process rather than optimization of closed-loop process, based on ecopoetic and relational biology approaches. The organizations would need to create new business models, measurement systems, and governing systems which would link economic incentives with ecological restoration. The model sees the supply chain as an agent for regeneration on a social level. As a conceptual framework, the propositions set out here need to be verified empirically across a range of industries and varied regional settings. No primary information was taken in, so every claim is only a theoretical proposal, plus an expected outcome, rather than a demonstrated result.

summary: The purpose of this study was to obtain empirical evidence and to examine the effect of the independent variables on firm size, firm financial leverage, firm age, audit quality, independent commissioners, managerial ownership, institutional ownership and profitability on earnings management as the dependent variable in non-financial companies that listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The method used in sampling is purposive sampling by determining five sample criteria and using multiple linear regression as a data analysis method. This study uses discretionary accruals which are calculated using the modified Jones model as a proxy for earnings management, natural logarithm to measure firm size variable, logarithm to measure firm age variable, audit quality variable and management ownership using dummy variable, and firm financial leverage variable, independent commissioner, institutional ownership and profitability are measured using a ratio scale. The results of this study indicate that firm size and profitability have an influence on earnings management, while firm age, firm financial leverage, audit quality, independent commissioners, managerial ownership and institutional ownership have no effect on earnings management.

title: Revolutionizing hospital supply chain: machine learning for predictive risk assessment
summary: Purpose The purpose of this study is to identify and prioritize the risks associated with healthcare supply chain with a focus on hospital’s internal supply chain. Design/methodology/approach The study presents a machine learning model for hospital supply chain risk assessment. Through previous literature and interviews, 35 risk factors were identified, which were then used to devise a questionnaire aimed at assessing the probability and impact of these risk factors. A total of 140 responses were gathered from subject matter experts. Six machine learning algorithms, namely, Naïve Bayes (NB), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) were used in this study. Techniques including holdout validation and k-fold cross-validation were used for evaluating the six classifiers. Findings Results from the feature subset selection process revealed that the most significant variables included “black market,” “delay in replacement of defective products,” “delay in delivery of imported products,” “defaulted suppliers,” “mismanagement of expired medicines,” “lack of planning,” “ban on import of raw materials” and “lack of budget.” While holdout validation results showed that Naïve Bayes achieved highest classification accuracy of 85.7%, the k-fold cross-validation indicated that RF, ANN and KNN outperformed NB, LR and SVM in terms of accuracy, highlighting their superior generalization capability. Originality/value The study fills an important research gap by providing valuable and novel insights for healthcare institutes and policymakers in making informed decisions regarding risk mitigation strategies, resource allocation and operational planning. By shifting their focus on the critical risk factors, stakeholders can prioritize their efforts and resources more effectively.

title: ANALYSIS OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF GREEN FINANCE IN THE CONTEXT OF TRANSFORMATION AND ECONOMIC GROWTH IN EU COUNTRIES
summary: The aim of the study was to examine the effectiveness of green finance in the context of transformational processes and economic growth in the European Union countries during 2015–2024. Specifically, the study contributes by testing how institutional maturity is associated with heterogeneous patterns in the relationship between green finance and macroeconomic outcomes across EU member states. The study analyzed the dynamics of investment in the green economy, the structure of financial instruments, the political initiatives of the European Union and their association with macroeconomic indicators. To ensure the comprehensiveness of the analysis, quantitative methods were applied, including correlation and regression analysis based on official statistical data from Eurostat, the European Central Bank and specialized agencies. It was observed that the total volume of green investments in the European Union increased by approximately 365%, from EUR 89 billion in 2015 to EUR 412 billion in 2024, while the volume of green bond issuance reached EUR 253.4 billion in 2024, according to the underlying datasets used in the analysis. Western and Northern European countries — in particular Germany, Sweden and France — demonstrated higher levels of observed green finance activity and related macroeconomic indicators. This was accompanied by an increase in the share of renewable energy to around 65% in selected country groups, alongside job creation estimates exceeding 400,000 in Germany according to reported statistical sources, and a reduction in the unemployment rate of approximately 1.2 percentage points annually after 2020 in the observed period. These patterns are reported as temporal associations rather than causal effects. In Central and Eastern European countries such as Poland and Hungary, lower levels of green investment activity were observed, which may be linked to structural constraints such as dependency on fossil fuels and slower energy infrastructure modernization. A positive correlation between green investment and GDP growth was identified: in countries with higher levels of institutional maturity, the correlation coefficient was above approximately 0.75 in the analyzed sample. The forecast to 2030 suggests a potential increase in green finance volumes up to approximately EUR 1.2 trillion under continued regulatory development scenarios, while macroeconomic outcomes are discussed as scenario-dependent projections rather than deterministic effects. The practical relevance of the findings lies in the potential to inform financing mechanisms for environmental projects, support sustainable growth strategies and contribute to discussions on macroeconomic stability at the level of EU countries.

title: Unmasking greenwashing through the role of gender diversity and CSR committees in driving real sustainability in Chinese firms
summary: Greenwashing, the deliberate overstatement of a firm’s environmental performance, undermines stakeholder trust and threatens the credibility of corporate sustainability reporting. This study examines how three board attributes, gender diversity, independence, and directors’ international experience, influence greenwashing among Chinese listed firms, and whether Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) committees strengthen these governance effects. Drawing on 4,312 firm-year observations from 2016 to 2023, sourced from the CSMAR, Bloomberg, and Refinitiv (Asset4) databases, greenwashing is measured as the gap between a firm’s disclosed and actual ESG performance. The results indicate that board gender diversity, independence, and international experience are each associated with lower greenwashing, and that CSR committees strengthen these effects, reinforcing corporate accountability and disclosure quality. These findings offer empirical evidence that internal governance mechanisms, not only external regulation, shape firms’ environmental integrity, with implications for policymakers and corporate leaders seeking to improve the credibility of ESG reporting.

title: Blockchain-based pharmaceutical supply chain: a scalable and transparent model for drug traceability
summary: An efficient Supply Chain Management (SCM) system is crucial for ensuring product quality, safety, and reliability. The pharmaceutical supply chain includes all processes from the collection of raw materials to the secure delivery of drugs to end consumers. However, traditional pharmaceutical SCM systems often suffer from limited transparency, traceability, scalability, and security, which increase drug counterfeiting and trust issues among stakeholders. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Blockchain-Based Pharmaceutical Supply Chain (BBPSC) management system. The proposed scheme records, monitors, and verifies every stage of the pharmaceutical supply chain while ensuring data security. It integrates Filecoin for decentralized off-chain data storage, the Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA) for cryptographic authentication, and Ethereum-based smart contracts to enable secure, immutable, and automated supply chain operations. In the proposed system, the Proof of Stake (PoS) consensus mechanism is used to validate transactions before they are included in the blockchain, thereby enhancing efficiency and reducing computational overhead. Informal and formal security analyses presented in this paper demonstrate the resilience of the proposed scheme against major security attacks. Experimental results indicate that the proposed BBPSC scheme outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of throughput, communication cost, deployment cost, latency, and scalability.

title: Are Corporate Governance Choices Contagious? Peer Effects in Board Gender Diversity and Institutional Ownership
summary: ABSTRACT This research explores whether corporate governance has a comprehensive impact on peer firms, analyzing US companies via a sample of 15,494 observations from 2001 to 2018. The findings reveal that effective corporate governance produces positive spillover effects, leading to better overall governance across the industry. Specifically, a rise in the proportion of female directors among peer firms positively increases female board representation in focal firms. Similar spillover effect is also observed in patterns of institutional ownership. However, the study reveals that imitating corporate governance practices of peers can ultimately be detrimental to the value and profitability of the imitating firms. Finally, our results also indicate that the peer effect in corporate governance is more pronounced among firms with lower R&D investments and those without financial resource limitations. These findings highlight that a firm's ability or willingness to imitate peers' corporate governance is shaped by its internal resources and strategic capacity.

title: The Political Economy of Energy Transitions in the Global South: Domestic Coalitions, State Capacity, and the Structural Constraints of Climate Finance 2. Authors
summary: Why do energy transitions in the Global South advance unevenly when renewable technologies are cost-competitive and international climate finance is on offer? I argue that outcomes depend on the interaction of two variables: the political settlement that determines whether incumbent fossil fuel interests are compensated, bypassed or displaced, and the position of the state within a hierarchical international financial system, which conditions whether external finance widens or narrows fiscal space. Using a structured, focused comparison of South Africa, India and the lithium-producing states of Chile, Argentina and Bolivia, based on official programme, audit, statistical and regulatory records, I identify three mechanisms. In South Africa, 42 per cent of USD 13.92 billion in Just Energy Transition Partnership pledges had been allocated by December 2025; sovereign policy loans were the only instrument allocated in full, while concessional loans intended for the state utility were held back by its borrowing restrictions. In India, nine state-owned energy firms invested INR 2.33 trillion in fossil fuels and INR 0.30 trillion in clean energy in fiscal year 2025, and state distribution companies returned to long-term coal contracts while about 42 GW of tendered renewable capacity lacked buyers. In the lithium triangle, the state's share of rents follows state capacity and business power, and remains exposed to a fall in the average price of battery-grade lithium carbonate from USD 63,700 per tonne in 2022 to USD 9,000 in 2025. The article shows how the composition and channel of climate finance, rather than its headline volume, shape domestic transition politics.

title: Investigating the Economic and Productivity Effects of Digital Transformation in Project Management
summary: Project management is being reshaped by artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, automation, data analytics, and digital project management platforms. Yet the expected economic and productivity gains are not always realized due to execution costs, skills gaps, integration challenges, and organizational resistance. This study analyses the effects of digital transformation on economic efficiency, productivity, workflow optimization, and project delivery, and examines the link between employee digital competency and transformation success. A mixed-methods design was used: a quantitative survey of 100 project employees and semi-structured interviews with 10 employees. Quantitative analysis employed frequencies, percentages, and descriptive statistics; qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Overall, perceptions of digital transformation were positive: 68%–78% agreed or strongly agreed that digital technologies improve cost efficiency, resource use, project performance, workflow efficiency, productivity, and delivery outcomes. Moreover, 74% associated higher employee digital competency with improved project results. Five themes emerged: economic efficiency and cost optimization; productivity and workflow optimization; employee digital competency; leadership and organizational culture; and data-driven decision-making and risk mitigation. Key hurdles remain: execution costs, resistance to change, skills gaps, and data quality. The study concludes that successful digital transformation depends on employee competence, effective leadership, organizational readiness, and disciplined execution conditions that can enhance project performance and economic value.

title: Green knowledge transaction networks, knowledge absorptive capacity and breakthrough green innovation
summary: Purpose Drawing on the knowledge-based view, structural holes theory and absorptive capacity theory, this study aims to examine how firms’ structural advantages in green knowledge transaction networks affect breakthrough green innovation. It further investigates the mechanisms through which knowledge retrieval ability, knowledge integration ability, and knowledge absorptive capacity shape this relationship. Design/methodology/approach This study measures the structural advantage of the green knowledge transaction network by the structural hole index and measures breakthrough green innovation by highly cited green invention patents within the same technology field. Findings The results show that structural advantages in green knowledge transaction networks are positively associated with breakthrough green innovation. This effect persists over time but gradually weakens. Mechanism tests indicate that knowledge retrieval ability and knowledge integration ability are important channels through which network structural advantages are transformed into breakthrough green innovation. The moderation results show that knowledge absorptive capacity strengthens the positive effect of green knowledge transaction network structural advantages on breakthrough green innovation. Further analysis shows that this effect is more pronounced in state-owned enterprises and firms in low-technology industries, while there is little difference in the effect between polluting and clean industries. Originality/value This study introduces green knowledge transaction networks into knowledge management research and incorporates knowledge retrieval ability, knowledge integration ability, and knowledge absorptive capacity into a unified analytical framework. It reveals the conversion logic through which green knowledge transaction networks affect breakthrough green innovation.

title: Research on the Influence of Green Credit Policy on Green Innovation of Heavy Polluting Enterprises
summary: This study examines the association between China’s 2012 Green Credit Guidelines and innovation among heavily polluting listed firms. Using panel data for Chinese A-share companies from 2006 to 2024, we compare firms in nine designated heavily polluting industries with other listed firms in a difference-in-differences framework. Green innovation is measured by green patent applications. We also examine patents identified as technologically novel because their four-digit International Patent Classification category had not appeared in the preceding five years. The baseline estimates show a positive association between the Guidelines and both patent measures. Additional analyses suggest that R&D investment may contribute to this relationship, although the evidence for this mechanism is limited. The estimated policy association is stronger among firms with lower operating expense ratios. Subgroup results indicate a larger association with green patent applications among state-owned firms and firms in eastern China, while the estimate for technologically novel patents is larger among non-state-owned firms. These subgroup comparisons should be interpreted cautiously because differences between their coefficients have not been formally tested. The findings offer evidence on how credit policy may shape firms’ innovation decisions, while the causal interpretation depends on the validity of the comparison-group and parallel-trends assumptions.

title: The impact of digital transformation and operational management on the financial performance of MSMEs in India
summary: The study investigates the impact of operational management and digital technology transformation on the financial performance of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in western India. This research examines the combined impact of these factors on the financial and operational outcomes of MSMEs, offering insights for business owners and policymakers. The study is based on empirical analysis of responses from 140 business owners and managers of MSMEs across industrial clusters in western India, using structured Likert scale questionnaires to assess relationships between operational management, technology transformation, and financial performance through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) analysis. Findings indicate that both constructs positively influence financial performance, with technology transformation showing a comparatively stronger effect. Businesses leveraging both effective operational strategies and digital tools experience higher profitability, return on assets, and return on investment. The study further reveals significant differences in operational and technological capabilities across firm size categories, with medium-sized enterprises outperforming micro and small enterprises. The geographical scope is limited to select industrial clusters in western India, and findings may not be generalizable across India given regional variation. The study emphasizes that MSMEs must integrate operational excellence with digital innovation to remain competitive in an evolving market.

title: Digital Social Administration: A New Paradigm for Understanding the Digital Transformation of Welfare
summary: ABSTRACT Digital public administration scholarship has expanded on broad trends in government digitalization, yet its generic categories, such as ‘citizen’, ‘user’ and ‘service’, systematically overlook what is distinctive about welfare administration. From automated debt recovery and predictive risk modelling to algorithmic child protection and emerging generative AI applications, the digital transformation of social policy creates profound dilemmas that generic frameworks cannot address. This paper proposes digital social administration (DSA) as a new conceptual paradigm—the ensemble of digitized and automated systems, data infrastructures, algorithmic tools and organizational practices through which welfare states assess eligibility, allocate benefits, govern risk and manage disadvantaged populations. We develop the TOV Three‐Dimensional Analytical Framework to operationalize this paradigm, focusing on the Technical, Organizational and Valuational dimensions of DSA and their relationships. Applying the framework to four signature dilemmas, and considering the emerging challenges posed by advanced AI and AGI demonstrates its ability to reveal dynamics that single‐dimensional approaches overlook. DSA constitutes a qualitatively new administrative form, comparable to the bureau‐professional state or new public management, and demands concepts adequate to its specificity. We conclude by outlining a research agenda organized around the TOV dimensions and identifying implications for social policy, practice, advocacy and legal reform.

title: Digital Transformation of Pharmaceutical Production Planning in Saudi Arabia Using Integrated ERP Systems
summary: Saudi Arabia is pursuing pharmaceutical localization, industrial diversification, health security, and digital transformation under Vision 2030. Yet local manufacturing capacity alone does not guarantee reliable medicine supply. Pharmaceutical plants must convert volatile demand, imported-material constraints, validated process capacity, quality-release requirements, and regulatory obligations into executable production plans. Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems can provide the digital backbone for this task, but value depends on integration with manufacturing execution, quality, laboratory, warehouse, maintenance, supplier, and advanced planning systems. This integrative review examines how ERP-enabled digital transformation can strengthen pharmaceutical production planning in Saudi Arabia. Recent pharmaceutical and Industry 4.0 literature is synthesized with Saudi policy and regulatory sources to identify planning capabilities, integration requirements, governance risks, and implementation priorities. The review argues that ERP should be treated not as an administrative transaction platform but as the controlled planning layer connecting demand, master production scheduling, material requirements planning, finite capacity, procurement, inventory, manufacturing execution, and batch release. A six-domain framework is proposed covering master-data integrity, integrated planning, execution visibility, quality-by-design information flows, analytics, and governance. The paper also presents an architecture for ERP-MES-QMS-LIMS-WMS-APS integration, a balanced KPI framework, and a phased 2026–2030 roadmap. For Saudi pharmaceutical manufacturers, the expected strategic value is improved schedule reliability, material readiness, capacity utilization, traceability, technology-transfer readiness, and resilience. The central conclusion is that digital transformation of planning should be built around validated processes, standardized data, cross-functional governance, and progressive integration rather than isolated technology deployment.

title: Exploring the Items for Measuring Flexible Supply Chain Management in the Organization in the Context of Nigeria: An Exploratory Factor Analysis
summary: The aim of this research to conduct instruments validation for the items of flexible supply chain management (FSCM) through exploratory factor analysis (EFA). The data collection tool employed is questionnaires which was administrated to employees in the manufacturing companies in Nigeria. 100 questionnaires were collected to do the EFA. The results reveal that the Bartlett’s Test of Sphericity was less that 0.05 ( 0.6) , and this indicates that the sample is adequate in size. Cronbach’s Alpha test was higher than 0.7 for the all the constructs items, this indicates that these items are all reliable. This study found a valid and reliable instrument for measuring the components of flexible supply chain management that could boost performance in manufacturing companies in Nigeria context. This study was applied to the manufacturing companies in Nigeria. This study adds to the measurement of the FSCM. This study contributes to the field of supply chain by evaluating and testing items that fit for testing the construct of flexible supply chain management.

title: ENHANCING SMALLHOLDER AND RETAILER COMPETITIVENESS THROUGH EFFICIENT AND DYNAMIC VEGETABLE SUPPLY CHAINS IN CAMBODIA
summary: The study examined strategies for improving the competitiveness of smallholder farmers and retailers through efficient and dynamic vegetable supply chains in Cambodia. The study was motivated by persistent challenges relating to fragmented marketing systems, inadequate post-harvest infrastructure, weak governance coordination, and limited market integration, which constrain the performance of the vegetable sector. The study was grounded in Dynamic Capabilities Theory, which explains how organisations and supply-chain actors develop, integrate, and reconfigure resources and capabilities to respond effectively to changing market conditions. The study was conducted using a mixed-methods research design that consisted of a cross-sectional survey of 420 smallholder vegetable producers, 85 key informant interviews, and six focus group discussions. The quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, multiple regression, ANOVA, and Structural Equation Modelling (SEM), while the qualitative data were analysed thematically. The results show that the respondents strongly agreed that efficient supply chains are important in improving competitiveness, household income, and retailer profitability. Supply-chain efficiency and governance coordination explained 66.3% of the variation in competitiveness (R2 = 0.663, R = 0.814), according to regression analysis. The regression model was statistically significant (F = 118.463; p < 0.001). Supply-chain efficiency had the strongest impact on competitiveness (β = 0.603, p < 0.001). Governance coordination improved supply-chain performance significantly (β = 0.384, p < 0.001). The SEM also revealed a significant positive effect of supply-chain efficiency on competitiveness (β = 0.684, p < 0.001) and governance coordination on supply-chain performance (β = 0.592, p < 0.001). The study found that efficient logistics, collaborative governance, digital innovation, market integration, and better post-harvest systems are essential to boost competitiveness. It is recommended that Cambodia develop resilient and sustainable vegetable supply chains through strengthening agricultural cooperatives, expanding cold-chain and storage infrastructure, promoting digital market information systems, improving stakeholder collaboration, and increasing government investment in supportive policies and rural infrastructure.

title: A data driven assessment of structural barriers to electrical equipment manufacturing in Bangladesh: trade dependency, industrial competitiveness, and policy pathways
summary: The rapid expansion of Bangladesh’s power and industrial sectors has led to a significant increase in demand for electrical equipment, a large portion of which is currently fulfilled through imports, resulting in sustained foreign currency outflows and supply chain vulnerabilities. This study investigates the feasibility, opportunities, and constraints associated with developing local assembly and manufacturing of electrical equipment, with particular focus on transformers and low- and medium-voltage panels. The analysis is based on a mixed-method approach that integrates foreign trade data from FY 2021–22 to FY 2023–24, industry-level information, and policy evaluation to assess import dependency, domestic manufacturing capability, and export potential. The findings reveal that the sector is characterized by high reliance on imported finished products and raw materials, indicating structural limitations in local value addition and technological capability. However, the study demonstrates that strengthening domestic manufacturing can significantly reduce import dependency, shorten procurement lead times, and enhance supply chain resilience while generating employment and supporting industrial skill development. Furthermore, the analysis identifies key fiscal and procurement policy reforms as critical enablers for improving cost competitiveness, facilitating import substitution, and unlocking export opportunities. title: Managerial perspectives on green innovation and technical efficiency in Caribbean Small Island Developing States
summary: The global transition toward environmental sustainability requires a private sector reorientation, yet the economic implications of green innovation remain inconsistent across institutional landscapes. This study examines how green innovation and underlying managerial motivations associate with firm production efficiency within the climate-vulnerable context of Caribbean Small Island Developing States (SIDS). Utilizing the 2020 Innovation, Firm Performance, and Gender dataset—a cross-sectional survey of 1979 enterprises across 13 Caribbean territories—the study employs Stochastic Frontier Analysis to estimate technical efficiency gap scores. Given the single-wave design collected during the COVID-19 pandemic shock, empirical findings are interpreted as exploratory baseline associations rather than definitive causal impacts. The results reveal a nuanced relationship: while general green innovation adoption is correlated with a technical efficiency penalty, innovations driven by environmental regulations and government financial incentives exhibit a significant positive statistical association with efficiency. Conversely, voluntary eco-innovations yield an efficiency penalty, while market-demand drivers display no significant relationship. These findings contribute to the Porter Hypothesis debate by demonstrating that green productivity offsets are not automatic in resource-constrained island economies. Instead, formal policy frameworks and financial de-risking mechanisms are essential for aligning environmental practices with operational productivity. Consequently, Caribbean governments should prioritize coordinated regulatory standards and targeted financial support to help private sector enterprises bridge the gap between sustainability and operational performance.

title: DATA VISUALIZATION AS A TOOL FOR UNDERSTANDABLE FINANCIAL REPORTING: EVIDENCE FROM BORSA ISTANBUL 30 FIRMS

title: THE EFFECT OF ESG PERFORMANCE ON SDG DISCLOSURE IN COMPANIES LISTED ON THE INDONESIA STOCK EXCHANGE IN 2021-2024
summary: Corporate transparency regarding the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) has emerged as a critical focal point in sustainability literature. Nevertheless, the inconsistent level of reporting among Indonesian firms suggests that the underlying drivers of this practice warrant deeper scrutiny. To address this gap, this investigation evaluates how Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance both as a composite metric and through its distinct pillars influences SDG-related reporting. Focusing on entities listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange from 2021 to 2024, the study utilized a purposive sampling approach to yield 232 firm-year observations, which were subsequently analyzed via panel data regression. The empirical outputs demonstrate that higher ESG scores, alongside robust performance in individual environmental, social, and governance areas, significantly boost the extent of SDG disclosures. Consequently, enterprises with superior sustainability records demonstrate a greater propensity for comprehensive non-financial reporting. This research enriches contemporary literature by offering granular empirical insights from an emerging economy, illustrating how multi-dimensional sustainability indicators shape corporate accountability.

title: Deflected disruption: payments and the taming of Chinese fintech
summary: Why and how do state authorities seek to deflect and harness technological disruption? Under what conditions do they shift between welcoming disruptive innovation as a driver of economic modernisation and seeing it as a threat to political and financial stability? We examine these questions in the context of how authorities handled the emergence of payments systems attached to digital platform companies within mainland China, where Ant Group and Tencent are used by over 1 billion people, and their international expansion to Southeast Asia. We argue that intermediation and the informational power derived from it are central to the political economy of Fintech disruption. Authorities and banking incumbents were accommodating of disruption to the extent it aligned with goals of increasing economic modernisation and efficiency. However, they were less tolerant of Fintech disruption that compromised their intermediary positions and informational power, and acted more strongly to deflect or block it. Similarly, Chinese fintechs in Southeast Asia have been limited by intense competition in target markets, as states in the region manage potential disruption of their international monetary orders. States are able to deflect the trajectory of Fintech disruption towards their own objectives, even if they cannot entirely stop or determine it.

title: A Digital Transformation Framework for AI-Enabled Electric Vehicle Charging in Smart Cities
summary: As cities move towards electrification and sustainability through the increased use of electric vehicles (EV), these new modes of mobility will continue to change urban transportation. However, deploying the required EV charged infrastructure at scale across large urban centers will introduce operational, technology and energy management complexities. This study offers a comprehensive digital transformation framework for AI-based EV charging systems that increase grid reliability, support user convenience and improve energy efficiency. This comprehensive framework facilitates the integration of AI and IoT connectivity via cloud-based platforms and smart grid technologies, thus creating an intelligent and adaptive system. The research has explored problems associated with dynamic load balancing, integrating renewable energy, predictive maintenance, and estimating demand in real-time. This study used a data-driven approach to optimize the EVs, charging stations, utilities, and city infrastructures with seamless communication through digital technologies. Additionally, further, this study examined the importance of utilizing digital platforms to build scalable infrastructure, increase cyber resilience, and create a user-centric service delivery model. Using simulation-based testing, the study has shown improved EV charging efficiencies and reductions in peak electrical loads and operational costs. This model allows policymakers, city planners, and energy providers to develop resilient, sustainable, and intelligent EV charging systems. Furthermore, this framework reaffirms a larger global vision of carbon-neutral smart cities powered by digitally enabled mobility ecosystems.

title: CEO TURNOVER AND VOLUNTARY AUDITOR SWITCHING: EVIDENCE FROM INDONESIAN MANUFACTURING FIRMS
summary: Voluntary auditor switching is an important phenomenon in corporate governance practices as it can affect audit quality and independence. This study aims to analyze the influence of audit opinion, financial distress, audit fees, and firm size on voluntary auditor switching, with CEO turnover as a moderating variable. The research employs panel data from 73 manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 20172023 period, resulting in a total of 511 annual observations. The analytical techniques used are logistic regression and moderated regression analysis (MRA). The results show that audit opinion, financial distress, and firm size significantly affect voluntary auditor switching, while audit fees have no effect. Furthermore, CEO turnover is proven to moderate the influence of audit opinion on voluntary auditor switching but does not moderate the relationship between financial distress, audit fees, and firm size with the decision to switch auditors. These findings provide implications for corporate stakeholders in considering internal factors and management changes when making audit decisions oriented toward enhancing accountability and transparency. title: Artificial Intelligence in Accounting-an over View
summary: AI is transforming accounting by automating processes such as financial reporting, data analysis, and decision-making. It improves accounting operations by leveraging a variety of technologies such as computer vision, natural language processing, and machine learning. title: Digging into disclosure: Mapping site-level publicly disclosed VSS engagement in lithium and cobalt mining
summary: The growing importance of critical minerals such as lithium and cobalt in the energy transition has intensified scrutiny over environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices in mining supply chains. While Voluntary Sustainability Standards (VSS) are increasingly used to signal responsible sourcing, publicly disclosed engagement with these standards at the mine-site level remains poorly documented. This study systematically maps publicly disclosed engagement with VSS across industrial lithium and cobalt mining operations and examines how these patterns vary geographically and by ownership structure. A global dataset of 117 industrial mining sites was compiled using 2023 production data from S&P Global Market Intelligence, company disclosures, official VSS databases (including IRMA and TSM), publicly available audit documentation, and other mine-site sources. Sites were analysed based on publicly disclosed VSS engagement, mine-site references to sustainability initiatives, and ownership structure using the headquarters country of the largest shareholder as a proxy for the geographical distribution of ownership. The results reveal a structural asymmetry in publicly disclosed VSS engagement: engagement is concentrated among a limited number of high-output sites, while most mine sites report no publicly disclosed VSS engagement. Lithium production is highly concentrated around IRMA, whereas cobalt exhibits a more fragmented governance landscape and substantially lower mine-site VSS engagement when supply-chain and smelter/refiner-level initiatives are excluded. These findings provide new empirical evidence on the uneven coverage of publicly disclosed VSS engagement and highlight the limitations of VSS as comprehensive governance tools in critical mineral supply chains. The results have implications for emerging due diligence regulations and highlight the need for improved transparency tools to support policy implementation.

title: Green finance moderates the association between foreign direct investment and green economic growth in Southeast Asian economies
summary: This study investigates how green finance (GF) moderates the relationship between foreign direct investment (FDI) and green economic growth (GEG) in seven Southeast Asian economies over 2013–2023. Using pooled OLS, fixed effects, random effects, and feasible generalized least squares (FGLS), we find that FDI and conventional financial development are negatively associated with GEG, whereas GF is positively associated with GEG. The FDI×GF interaction is positive and statistically significant, indicating that higher GF attenuates the negative FDI-GEG association. A support-aware marginal-effect check shows that the implied zero crossing occurs at GF = 30.5 on the ln(1 + investment) scale, far outside the observed GF range of 0–7.04; therefore, the data do not support an in-sample sign reversal or an actionable monetary threshold. Sensitivity checks using an alternative dependent variable and time fixed effects preserve the direction of the principal coefficients. The findings contribute by integrating FDI, financial development, and green finance in a single ASEAN framework and by showing that green finance can mitigate, although not reverse within the observed sample, the adverse association between FDI and green economic growth.

title: STRUKTUR KEPEMILIKAN DAN PENGUNGKAPAN ESG
summary: This study aims to analyze the impact of ownership structure on the level of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure. The ownership structures in this study include managerial, institutional, family, majority, and government ownership. ESG is considered an important indicator in reflecting a company's commitment to sustainability and social responsibility in the modern business era. These ownership structures have varying impacts on ESG disclosure based on agency theory. This study uses a quantitative approach to test the hypothesis. This study has a population of non-financial companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2021 to 2024. The study sample consists of 364 company-years. The results of multiple linear regression analysis indicate that managerial and institutional ownership do not affect ESG disclosure. Family and majority ownership have a negative effect on ESG disclosure. Government ownership has a positive effect on ESG disclosure. The control variables in this study are profitability, company size, and leverage. Profitability and leverage do not affect ESG disclosure. Company size has a positive effect on ESG disclosure. The findings of this study have the following implications: first, companies with majority and family ownership tend to withhold strategic information, such as ESG, to protect their interests (entrenchment effect). Second, state-owned enterprises face high public pressure, which leads to increased compliance with ESG disclosures. Third, managerial and institutional ownership do not reduce information asymmetry

title: Extrapolating CSR–HRM interdependencies and employee well-being for sustainable workplaces in generative AI era
summary: The development of generative AI (GAI) capabilities has led corporate entities to rethink their strategic initiatives towards sustainable workforce management. This dynamism has been broadly identified as a concern for managerial teams. Despite strong consensus on the roles of organizational human resources and corporate governance in managing the deployment of GAI mechanisms, specific factors contributing to each orientation remain unidentified. The current study addresses this gap by conducting a comprehensive review of factors that may affect sustainability orientation and employee well-being in the context of GAI implementation. The study utilized total interpretive structural modeling (TISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to the classification (MICMAC) method to develop the hierarchical relationship model. The study identified 16 factors: nine attributed to human resource management (HRM) and seven to the corporate social responsibility (CSR) domain. The study develops an expert-informed structural representation of the interrelationships between the two categories of designated factors. The outcomes identify two foundational factors as independent drivers and one dependent factor related to the social assessment of technology from a CSR perspective. The findings provide a structured interpretation of the interdependence between HRM and CSR factors and their implications for sustainable workforce management and employee health in SMEs. The study offers novel managerial implications on the relative orientations of driving and dependency factors for managing a sustainable workforce while supporting new technology development in the SME context.
