title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Green Logistics: Implications for Sustainable Supply Chain Performance in Nigeria's Transportation Sector
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming transportation and logistics by enabling data-driven decision-making, operational efficiency, and environmentally sustainable practices. However, the adoption of AI-enabled green logistics remains limited in Nigeria due to inadequate digital infrastructure, high implementation costs, limited technical expertise, weak institutional support, and regulatory challenges. This study examines how AI adoption influences green logistics practices and sustainable supply chain performance in Nigeria’s transportation and logistics sector. The study adopted a qualitative multiple-case study design involving four purposively selected organizations representing road freight and distribution, maritime and port-related logistics, third-party logistics, and integrated logistics services. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 24 key informants and analysed using thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke’s six-phase approach, with evidence examined at both within-case and cross-case levels. The findings indicate that AI applications, including predictive analytics, machine learning, intelligent route optimization, demand forecasting, and AI-enabled warehouse management, improve resource efficiency, supply chain visibility, fleet utilization, and operational responsiveness while reducing fuel consumption, waste, and environmental emissions. However, inadequate digital infrastructure, unreliable electricity, limited data quality, high implementation costs, cybersecurity concerns, and insufficient regulatory support constrain wider adoption. The study concludes that AI can strengthen green logistics and sustainable supply chain performance when supported by organisational readiness and enabling technological and institutional environments. It recommends investment in digital infrastructure, workforce capacity, AI governance, supportive policies, and public-private partnerships to accelerate sustainable logistics transformation and contribute to the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 9, 11, 12, 13, and 17 in Nigeria.

title: Ownership structure and firm performance in G5 countries: a dynamic panel ARDL approach with a focus on employee shareholding
summary: Purpose This study examines how institutional, concentrated and employee ownership structures impact the financial performance of publicly listed firms across G5 countries. It aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of how different ownership types influence firm performance metrics (ROA and Tobin's Q) while addressing gaps in existing literature regar, Faculty of Economic Sciences and Management of Tunis ding comparative cross-country analysis and the underexplored role of employee ownership. Design/methodology/approach The research utilizes panel data from 550 firms across G5 nations spanning 2016–2023. The methodology centers on the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) model using the pooled mean group (PMG) estimator, which accommodates mixed-order integration of variables and enables simultaneous examination of short-run adjustments and long-run relationships. Robustness checks include panel unit root tests and cointegration analysis. Findings The analysis reveals that employee shareholding has a significant positive long-run relationship with firm profitability, though no short-term effect. For institutional ownership no significant impact on profitability was found in either the long or short run. Conversely, majority shareholder ownership demonstrates a significant positive long-term association with firm profitability but an insignificant short-term effect. Practical implications The findings offer useful implications for corporate governance. The positive effect of ownership concentration suggests that large shareholders can enhance monitoring and reduce agency conflicts, thereby improving firm performance. In contrast, the insignificant impact of institutional ownership indicates limited monitoring by institutional investors. This highlights the need to encourage more active institutional investor participation in corporate governance. Originality/value This research represents the first comprehensive application of ARDL panel techniques to simultaneously analyze all three ownership types across major economies. It systematically incorporates employee ownership into performance analysis, an aspect frequently overlooked in financial research. The comparative framework across G5 countries reveals how institutional contexts moderate ownership-performance relationships, particularly showing stronger employee ownership effects in coordinated market economies.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES, AND IMPLICATIONS FOR SERVICE QUALITY
summary: The tourism and hospitality sector is experiencing a rapid digital transformation driven by artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, mobile technologies, automation, and increasingly connected service environments. These technologies are changing how travellers search for information, select accommodation, communicate with service providers, and evaluate their experiences. At the same time, hotels and tourism enterprises are using digital tools to improve operational efficiency, personalise services, support employees, and make decisions based on data. This article examines the main opportunities and challenges associated with AI and digital transformation in tourism and hospitality, with particular attention to service quality and the role of human employees. The paper uses a narrative review of recent international research and policy literature. The analysis indicates that AI can support customer communication, demand forecasting, recommendation systems, revenue management, multilingual assistance, and routine operational tasks. However, successful digital transformation depends not only on technology but also on employee skills, data governance, privacy protection, service design, and the preservation of meaningful human interaction. The article argues that technology should be implemented as a tool for strengthening hospitality rather than as a substitute for hospitality itself. The findings are relevant to hospitality managers, tourism educators, students, and policymakers seeking to prepare the sector for a more digital and data-informed future.

title: Methodological Evaluation and Reliability Forecasting for District Hospital Systems in Ethiopia: A Time-Series Meta-Analysis
summary: District hospitals are critical nodes in healthcare delivery, yet systematic evaluations of their operational reliability in low-resource settings are scarce. Existing assessments often lack robust, predictive methodologies to inform proactive system strengthening. This meta-analysis aims to methodologically evaluate published and grey literature on district hospital systems in Ethiopia and to develop a time-series forecasting model for predicting system reliability. We conducted a systematic search for time-series and longitudinal studies reporting on hospital operational metrics. A bespoke Bayesian structural time-series model was fitted to synthesise data, forecasting reliability as a function of infrastructural, staffing, and supply chain covariates. The core forecasting equation is $R_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{t-1} + \phi R_{t-1} + \epsilon_t$, where $R_t$ is reliability. Model uncertainty was quantified using 95% credible intervals. The methodological review identified a predominant focus on static snapshots rather than dynamic analysis. The forecasting model indicates a strong positive association between supply chain continuity and predicted reliability, with a one-standard-deviation improvement in supply metrics increasing forecasted reliability by 15.2 percentage points (95% CrI: 11.8 to 18.6). The analysis demonstrates the feasibility and utility of applying time-series meta-analytic forecasting to hospital system evaluation, revealing key dynamic drivers of reliability often obscured in cross-sectional studies. Future research and monitoring should adopt longitudinal designs to capture system dynamics. title: The Influence of Debt to Equity Ratio (DER) and Good Corporate Governance on Company Value at PT Gudang Garam TBK for the Period 2015 - 2025
summary: This research aims to investigate the impact of the Debt to Equity Ratio (DER) and Good Corporate Governance (proxied by Board of Directors Size) on Firm Value (Tobin's Q) at PT Gudang Garam Tbk. The research design employs a quantitative descriptive and causal associative approach, using time-series historical financial statements over the 2015–2025 period. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression assisted by IBM SPSS 27. Empirical results prove that, simultaneously, DER and Board of Directors Size significantly influence Firm Value (F-value = 7.802; Sig. = 0.013) with a determination coefficient of 66.1%. However, partial testing reveals an anomaly where the Debt to Equity Ratio has no significant effect (t-value = 1.223; Sig. = 0.256), indicating that the company's market share dominance leads rational investors to discount debt fluctuations. Conversely, Board of Directors Size exhibits a significant negative impact (t-value = -2.500; Sig. = 0.037), where an oversized board configuration is perceived to create bureaucratic inefficiency (Agency Theory).

title: Life cycle and techno-economic assessment of anion exchange membrane electrolysis: Cradle-to-gate supply chain emissions and scale-dependent cost analysis
summary: This study presents an integrated assessment of anion exchange membrane electrolysis that combines experimentally validated lifecycle inventory data, comprehensive cradle-to-gate greenhouse gas accounting, and probabilistic techno-economic analysis under scale-dependent conditions. The results demonstrate that under a realistic Net Zero 2050 grid scenario, the total carbon footprint is estimated at 2.53 kgCO 2 eq/kgH 2 , with electricity consumption dominating the environmental impact. However, evaluating the system under an ideal zero‑carbon electricity supply reveals a baseline footprint of 0.44 kgCO 2 eq/kgH 2 , demonstrating that upstream material production and component manufacturing impose an irreducible minimum emission threshold. Economically, the levelized cost of hydrogen decreases from $8.16/kgH 2 at a production scale of 1,000 kgH 2 /day to $5.05/kgH 2 at 50,000 kgH 2 /day, driven primarily by economies of scale. Notably, the two-parameter interaction analysis reveals that system availability and electrochemical efficiency act as primary co-optimization drivers, exhibiting a pronounced synergistic interaction for global warming potential while delivering additive economic benefits for hydrogen production cost. Furthermore, increasing system scale not only lowers costs but also progressively narrows economic uncertainty. These findings highlight that the sustainability of green hydrogen cannot be accurately evaluated without incorporating upstream supply chain impacts alongside operational metrics. The study provides an evidence-based framework for evaluating emerging electrolysis technologies and informing rigorous carbon certification standards.

title: Indoor environment supply chain management: Connecting digital data flow influencing sustainable development goals and knowledge dissemination
summary: This study aims to examine the impact of indoor environment, organizational culture, knowledge management, and data flow on academic library service quality within Chinese universities. It further investigates the mediating roles of supply chain integration and intellectual exports, as well as the moderating role of sustainable development goals (SDGs) orientation in strengthening service performance outcomes. A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured survey administered to academic library professionals in Chinese higher education institutions. A total of 245 valid responses were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling with SmartPLS. Reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and structural relationships were assessed through bootstrapping procedures to test direct, indirect, and moderating effects. The results reveal that the indoor environment, organizational culture, knowledge management, and data flow significantly and positively influence academic library service quality. Supply chain integration and intellectual exports partially mediate these relationships. Additionally, SDGs orientation strengthens the effects of supply chain integration and intellectual exports on service quality. This study proposes and validates an integrated, multi-layered framework that combines organizational, environmental, operational, intellectual, and sustainability dimensions to explain service quality in academic libraries. The findings offer strategic insights for enhancing library performance and sustainability alignment (SDGs) in higher education institutions.

title: INNOVATION IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: INVESTIGATING THE BIDIRECTIONAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TECHNOLOGICAL INNOVATION AND DIGITAL SERVICES TRADE
summary: This study examines the bidirectional relationship between digital services trade and technological innovation, as well as the distinct dynamics of the relationship between exports and imports. Using a three-stage least squares estimation approach on panel data from 83 economies from 2014 to 2021, findings reveal a positive and statistically significant two-way relationship between digital services trade and innovation output. Exports and imports of digital services are positively associated with technological innovation, and innovation corresponds positively to the digital services trade. While innovation exerts a substantial and elastic relationship with digital trade, the association between trade and innovation is modest and inelastic. Moreover, innovation has a stronger relationship with digital services exports than with imports, while imports exert a more pronounced link with innovation than exports. The findings imply policy priorities on financial access support, institutional quality, human capital, digital infrastructure and balanced regulations to foster innovation and digital services trade.

title: Litmus: Evaluating the Resilience of Blockchain-Enabled Software Systems for Supply Chains via Architecture Modeling and Chaos Injection
summary: Resilience is vital to blockchain-enabled software systems for supply chains (ChainFusion) and enables them to automatically adapt and continue providing their service when adverse situations occur. Since the notion of resilience in ChainFusion encompasses both the characteristics of a blockchain-enabled software system and the features of supply chains, complex trade-offs often exist among its resilience metrics. Furthermore, while blockchain technology provides novel mechanisms for enhancing resilience, it also inevitably introduces new resilience-related challenges. Therefore, when evaluating the resilience, it is crucial to evaluate the impact of blockchain technology on its resilience. In this paper, we propose Litmus, a method for evaluating the resilience of Chain-Fusion via architecture modeling and chaos injection. Litmus first models the system architecture using activity diagrams and extracts the minimal paths of the business process. Litmus then evaluates the resilience and outputs resilience issues by continuously injecting chaos into the system and monitoring variations in system state resilience curve. We assess the quality of Litmus by comparison with related work and through ablation experiments. We conduct case studies on a shipbuilding supply chain to evaluate the effectiveness of Litmus. Litmus identifies three previously unknown potential resilience issues. title: ACCOUNTING INFORMATION SYSTEMS AND THE FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES: EVIDENCE FROM ISTANBUL MARKET, ERIGAVO, SOMALILAND, FOR DECENT WORK, ECONOMIC GROWTH, AND INNOVATION
summary: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are the main source of decent work and economic growth in Somaliland, yet most still rely on informal, manual bookkeeping that weakens financial control, decision-making, and profitability, and no empirical evidence exists on accounting information systems (AIS) in Erigavo. This study examines the effect of four AIS components, namely record-keeping, financial reporting, budgetary control, and cash management systems, on the financial performance of SMEs operating in Istanbul Market, Erigavo District. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model, the Decomposed Theory of Planned Behavior, and Agency Theory, the study employs a census of all 20 AIS-using SMEs in the market and their 60 owners, managers, and employees; primary data were collected through a structured five-point Likert questionnaire and analyzed in SPSS using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression. Cronbach's alpha ranged from 0.797 to 0.834, confirming reliability. The results show that the four AIS components jointly explain 55.8% of the variance in financial performance (R = 0.747, R² = 0.558, adjusted R² = 0.526, F(4, 55) = 17.374, p < 0.001). Record-keeping systems were the strongest predictor (B = 0.529, β = 0.484, p < 0.001), followed by cash management systems (B = 0.459, β = 0.241, p = 0.039), financial reporting systems (B = 0.128, β = 0.083, p = 0.037), and budgetary control systems (B = 0.089, β = 0.070, p = 0.043). The findings suggest that a formalized AIS is a decisive, innovation-driven determinant of SME profitability and competitiveness in a fragile, cash-based economy, with transaction-level records and liquidity controls mattering more than periodic reporting and budgeting, thereby supporting industry, innovation, and infrastructure and sustainable economic growth.

title: Does Economic Policy Uncertainty Influence ESG Performance? Evidence from European Banking Sector
summary: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the impact of economic policy uncertainty (EPU) on environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance in the European banking sector and then to investigate the moderating influence of board gender diversity (BGD) on this relationship. We analyzed a sample of 113 European Union banks for the period 2016-2024 and we developed an econometric model applying a dynamic panel data regression analysis (generalized Method of Moments – GMM System) on 1,017 bank-year observations. To test research hypotheses, we considered BGD in terms of female participation on the board of directors and we measured ESG dimensions by using the ESG score provided by LSEG Refinitiv. The results highlight that EPU affects the ESG performance of European banks and specifically, demonstrate that EPU reduces the overall ESG score. EPU also declines governance and environmental engagements but enhances the social activities to dampen uncertainty during periods of high EPU. This study also suggests that the presence of women on board mitigate these negative effects since the influence of EPU on overall ESG performance is positive in this circumstance. The investigation is highly relevant for regulators, policymakers, potential investors, managers and other stakeholders who are interested in improving the ESG performance of banks under different uncertainties. In this regard, the study represents a significant avenue for future research, with relevant implications for both theory and practice. Our study significantly contributes to the existing literature on the relationship between EPU and ESG in developed countries such as the European context. In this regard, our research is the first that offers insights about the influence of the EPU on ESG performance in the European banking sector.

title: ESG Investing and Investor Behavioural Biases: A Systematic Review and Integrated Behavioural Finance Framework: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: This paper presents systematic literature review (SLR) based on the PRISMA framework on the nexus of ESG and investor behavioural biases in the stock market. The selection of 72 studies that fulfilled all the eligibility criteria was drawn from an initial sample of 5213 from Scopus, Web of Science, and additional databases, and synthesised thematically. It considers the interplay between cognitive and emotional biases (such as herding, overconfidence, disposition effect, loss aversion, confirmation bias, anchoring) and the quality of the ESG disclosure, rating divergence, and the perception of greenwashing to influence investment behaviour. The results show that investor psychology and financial expertise, as well as market conditions, play a significant role in determining the impact of ESG factors, which do not seem to work on a strictly rational and informational basis. On this synthesis, the paper lays out a new Integrated Behavioural Finance Framework, where the quality of the signals is proposed as an antecedent of the heuristic process and a set of testable propositions for future empirical research. The review reveals several limitations, including geographic underrepresentation (especially the GCC), biases of anchoring and regret aversion, and the lack of experimental and debiasing intervention studies. Implications are provided for investors, financial advisors, regulators and researchers interested in modelling sustainable investment decision making in a behaviourally realistic way. Findings: The review indicates that the impact of ESG on stock market investment decisions is mediated by behaviour and not just information. Investor behaviour is influenced by the interplay between the quality of ESG disclosure and rating divergence, as well as perceptions of greenwashing and the disposition effect, and overconfidence and herding. Institutional investors seem to distinguish between ESG dimensions based on the materiality of the sector and are generally less prone than retail investors to be biased in their processing of ESG information, who are more liable to herding and greenwashing risk. Higher divergence due to rating, coupled with higher voluntary disclosure, paradoxically increases (not resolves) the divergence, irrespective of the performance of the firms. Originality and Value: The novelty of this paper is that it combines in a systematic way two streams of literature in a PRISMA-based synthesis, instead of tackling the investor psychology and the quality of the ESG disclosure separately. It presents an Integrated Behavioural Finance Framework where signal quality is an antecedent to heuristic processing, that is moderated by investor-level and market-level variables, and testable propositions for future empirical testing. The review contributes to the field by pointing to Islamic finance's values-based screening logic, indicating that the GCC is a hugely under-researched context, and revealing gaps in methods and studies that have informed future research, including a lack of experimental debiasing studies.

title: The Role of Ownership Structure and Real Earnings Management on the Firm Performance of Non-Financial Firms Listed in Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
summary: This study investigates the impact of real earnings management (REM) on firm performance and the moderating role of ownership structure among non-financial firms listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). Grounded in agency and stakeholder theories, the research examines how different forms of ownership specifically managerial and institutional shape the relationship between REM and firm profitability, measured through Return on Assets (ROA). Using panel data from 2008 to 2023, the study employs a dynamic panel regression model to control for firm-specific effects and potential endogeneity. The findings reveal that REM positively influences short-term profitability, but its effect is significantly moderated by ownership structure. Managerial ownership enhances overall firm performance but intensifies the negative impact of REM on ROA, suggesting potential overuse or ineffective application of REM strategies when managers hold significant equity stakes. Conversely, institutional ownership not only directly improves profitability but also weakens the positive impact of REM, reflecting its governance role in constraining opportunistic managerial behavior. These results highlight the dual influence of ownership structure in both enhancing firm performance and regulating earnings management practices. The study offers valuable insights for corporate managers, investors, and policymakers on the importance of tailoring governance mechanisms to mitigate REM risks and ensure sustainable financial performance.

title: Transition Design for a Sustainable Meat and Alternatives Supply Chain in Japan: Three Transition Scenarios Envisioning Future Food Systems
summary: This study explores the transition toward a sustainable meat and alternative protein supply chain in Japan using a transition design approach. Amid growing global demands for sustainability in livestock systems, Japan faces unique challenges, such as geographical and structural constraints and low consumer awareness regarding sustainability and animal welfare. The aim of this study is to address the structural issues within Japan’s protein supply system and present sustainable transition scenarios. Through detailed interviews with 21 frontrunners and co-creation workshops, the structural challenges of the current socio-technical regime that hinder transition were analyzed, and a theory of change was developed. The findings reveal that Japan’s meat and protein supply systems are locked into unsustainable practices due to regulatory, cognitive, and normative rules. Based on these insights, three transition scenarios are proposed: “Grazed Lean Beef as a Feast,” “Localized Circular Communities,” and “Food Printer”. These scenarios emphasize the importance of experimental networks, culturally grounded visions, and phased interventions. This study contributes to the theoretical understanding of sustainable transitions in the food sector and provides practical strategies for policymakers and industry stakeholders in Japan.

title: Winning Consumer Trust Through Supply Chain Responsibility Communication: How Certification, Disclosure, and Beneficiary Framing Shape Credibility
summary: ABSTRACT As stakeholders increasingly demand supply chain transparency, companies face a legitimacy paradox: disclosing supply chain responsibility (SR) information is necessary to meet stakeholder expectations, yet disclosure can invite scrutiny rather than build credibility. Drawing on and extending legitimacy theory, this study investigates which attributes of SR communication resolve this paradox by enhancing credibility among consumers. Three vignette‐based experimental studies manipulate key attributes: disclosure presence, certification source, disclosure basis, metric focus, and beneficiary emphasis. Results show that SR communication significantly enhances perceived credibility compared to no communication, with social responsibility generating stronger effects than environmental responsibility—an asymmetry that disappears once communication is framed around worker rather than firm benefits. Third‐party certification substantially increases credibility compared to self‐certification, but this advantage diminishes when companies report relevant, verifiable outcomes, revealing that structural and consequential forms of legitimacy can substitute for one another. Contrary to expectations, voluntary disclosure does not enhance credibility over mandatory disclosure. Most notably, emphasizing benefits for supply chain workers generates significantly higher credibility than emphasizing benefits for the buying company, demonstrating the moral power of other‐oriented communication. The study extends legitimacy theory to consumer evaluations of supply chain practices, showing how companies can resolve the legitimacy paradox through specific communication design choices, and offers actionable guidance: companies should prioritize third‐party certification when outcome evidence is unavailable, and emphasize worker welfare over operational benefits.

title: Innovative Educational Technologies in Education amid Digital Transformation and Societal Change: A Socio-Pedagogical Alignment Framework
summary: Thesis. Innovative educational technologies should be interpreted as socio-pedagogical instruments whose educational value is determined not by technological novelty itself, but by their alignment with the criteria of pedagogical relevance, inclusive access, learner agency, support capacity and ethical governance. Concept. The article employs a conceptual review and analytical synthesis of scholarship on digital transformation, Education 4.0 and Education 5.0, technology-enhanced learning, digital inclusion, teacher competence, learner agency and educational data ethics. This synthesis underpins a framework for evaluating technology use amid societal change. Results and conclusions. The proposed Socio-Pedagogical Alignment Framework integrates macro-level societal and policy conditions, meso-level institutional and pedagogical conditions, and micro-level learner-centred conditions. Across these levels, five evaluative criteria structure evidence-based judgement: pedagogical relevance, inclusive access, learner agency, support capacity and ethical governance. The framework distinguishes three context-sensitive decision pathways: adoption, redesign and reassessment, or deferral or rejection. The framework advances a human-centred model of educational acceptability that enables innovative technologies to be assessed as conditional educational possibilities requiring pedagogical, social, institutional and ethical justification before implementation and subsequent validation.

title: Audited Operational Realisability: Canonical Inference Closure and Evidence-Preserving Composition
summary: Conditional mathematical arguments need careful bookkeeping: which obligations were incurred, which have been addressed, and which were addressed in a way that actually proves the target. Audited Operational Realisability (AOR) is a mathematical theory of this bookkeeping. An audit state consists of demanded records and stored certificates; each certificate carries a status, such as budgeted or blocked, and a payload whose meaning is fixed in advance. We separate three conclusions that are easily conflated. Inference closure registers every dependency of a demanded record, accounting requires a stored certificate for each demanded or dependency-reachable record, and delivery requires a certificate whose status an explicit consumer policy accepts as proving its target. A certificate recording that a budget is exceeded accounts for the obligation but does not deliver feasibility to a consumer who requires it. We prove that inference closure is a reflection that creates no evidence, in a category whose arrows preserve certificates exactly, and that this category has colimits in which every accepted certificate is already stored at some object of the diagram. For operations that add evidence, we prove finite completion under a decreasing rank and confluence under replayability, and we strictly separate accounting, recoverability, and uniform quantitative control. Retained evidence passes to increasing unions, and witnesses pass to limits under compactness and closed validity, provided an accepted payload is returned at the limit; without compactness they may escape. Two examples mark the boundary of accounting: a query system that pays its declared costs, is accounted, and identifies each hidden world along its exhaustive run, yet admits no finite-stage guarantee uniform over all worlds; and a Lipschitz target whose shrinking finite-prefix certificates, priced within a summable credit, are all accepted, with centers converging to the target. The stated structural results are formalized in Lean 4; the analytic estimates of applications remain explicit hypotheses.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF ELECTRICAL TRANSMISSION INFRASTRUCTURE THROUGH SMART GRID TECHNOLOGIES: A SAUDI VISION 2030 PERSPECTIVE
summary: Electricity transmission networks are changing from being based on individual assets to becoming systems that can be observed digitally, are driven by data and are becoming more adaptive. This shift is particularly important for Saudi Arabia, since the rapid expansion of renewable energy, the great distances across the country, the emergence of new industrial loads and the aims set out in Vision 2030 all mean that the transmission system has to handle greater variability without compromising reliability. This review carefully brings together 30 peer-reviewed studies that were published between 2020 and 2025 in order to look at how smart grid technologies can help with the digital transformation of the transmission infrastructure. The evidence is grouped into five interrelated areas of capability: wide area observability and digital substations; high-performance communications and edge-cloud computing; artificial intelligence and advanced analytics; digital twins and condition-based asset management; and flexibility technologies backed by storage, demand response and grid-enhancing measures. The review concludes that value is not obtained simply by acquiring individual technologies; instead, the benefits come about through the use of interoperable data models, time-synchronized measurements, cyber-resilient communication, validated analytics, coordinated control and governance structures that enable reliable operational decisions to be made on the basis of data.

title: Digital Transformation, Green Logistics Capability, and Operational Efficiency in Indonesian Freight Forwarding: The Sequential Mediating Mechanisms of Technology Adoption and Service Excellence
summary: This study examines the sequential mediating roles of technology adoption and service excellence in the relationships among digital transformation, green logistics capability, and operational efficiency in Indonesian freight forwarding companies. This quantitative causal-explanatory research employed a cross-sectional survey of 250 managers from freight forwarding companies in Indonesia. Data analysis utilized Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4.0 and bootstrapping with 5,000 subsamples. Data analysis utilized Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 3.0 and bootstrapping with 5,000 subsamples. The findings confirm all seven direct hypotheses and both sequential mediation hypotheses. Digital transformation significantly influences technology adoption (β=0.385, p<0.001), while green logistics capability positively affects technology adoption (β=0.342, p<0.001). Technology adoption substantially enhances service excellence (β=0.431, p<0.001), which in turn drives operational efficiency (β=0.402, p<0.001). Crucially, the sequential mediation pathways—digital transformation → technology adoption → service excellence → operational efficiency and green logistics capability → technology adoption → service excellence → operational efficiency—are both significant, demonstrating that technology adoption and service excellence function as complementary sequential mechanisms. This research provides theoretical contributions by extending dynamic capabilities theory through the identification of sequential micro-foundations and offers practical implications for forwarding managers, industry associations, and policymakers regarding integrated digital and green strategies.

title: Governance, CSR, and Leverage on Financial Distress in Indonesian Consumer Cyclicals
summary: Fluctuations in macroeconomic conditions and consumer purchasing capacity render firms in the consumer cyclical sector particularly susceptible to financial distress. Although the sector's index posted an upward trajectory throughout the observation window, such aggregate expansion offers no assurance that individual issuers maintain sound financial footing. Drawing on 116 firm-year observations from 29 consumer cyclical firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange across 2022-2025, this inquiry appraises how institutional ownership, independent commissioners, audit committee independence, corporate social responsibility (CSR) disclosure, and leverage relate to financial distress, operationalized through the Altman Z-Score, wherein elevated values signify a more robust financial standing and diminished vulnerability to failure. Sample selection followed a purposive sampling scheme, with panel-data regression estimated under a random-effects specification. Findings reveal that institutional ownership, independent commissioners, audit committee independence, and CSR disclosure bear no discernible statistical linkage to the Z-Score, whereas leverage registers a pronounced inverse relationship, implying that intensified debt reliance coincides with a depressed Z-Score and heightened distress exposure. Jointly, the five predictors exert a collectively significant influence on Z-Score variation, underscoring the ambiguous role of governance and CSR mechanisms while positioning leverage as the most consequential determinant of financial vulnerability among the firms examined

title: Green Financial Literacy and ESG Awareness to Sustainable Investment Intention: The Mediating Role of Green Trust
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of Green Financial Literacy and ESG Awareness on Sustainable Investment Intention and to examine the role of Green Trust as a mediating variable among young investors in Indonesia. The study employs a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional survey design. Data were obtained through an online survey of 327 investors aged 18–40 years holding a Single Investor Identification (SID). Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. Results indicate that Green Financial Literacy positively and significantly influences Green Trust (β = 0.348; p < 0.001), as does ESG Awareness on Green Trust (β = 0.326; p < 0.001). Green Trust emerges as the strongest direct predictor of Sustainable Investment Intention (β = 0.438; p < 0.001). Furthermore, Green Financial Literacy (β = 0.154; p = 0.004) and ESG Awareness (β = 0.142; p = 0.008) positively and significantly influence Sustainable Investment Intention directly. Green Trust also mediates the relationship between Green Financial Literacy and Sustainable Investment Intention (indirect effect = 0.152; p < 0.001) and between ESG Awareness and Sustainable Investment Intention (indirect effect = 0.143; p < 0.001). The model explains 41.2% of the variance in Green Trust and 52.7% of the variance in Sustainable Investment Intention. This study contributes to the literature by examining Green Financial Literacy as a sustainability-specific construct, identifying Green Trust as a mechanism connecting cognitive factors with sustainable investment intention, and providing empirical evidence from the context of young Indonesian investors. Findings suggest that knowledge and ESG awareness are not fully translated into investment intention without trust in the credibility of the sustainable financial ecosystem. These findings indicate that increasing sustainable investment requires a combination of strengthening green financial literacy and building trust. Financial institutions need to enhance education regarding sustainable financial products and ESG information transparency, while regulators need to strengthen ESG disclosure standardization and oversight of greenwashing practices. These efforts can strengthen investor trust and support the growth of sustainable investment in Indonesia.

title: Digital Transformation in Small-scale Food Enterprises: How Young Women Leverage Social Commerce to Globalize Local Specialties
summary: This study examines how digital transformation contributes to market expansion performance among young women-led small-scale food enterprises in Vietnam, with social commerce proposed as a mediating mechanism and digital literacy as a moderating capability. Drawing on the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study conceptualizes market expansion performance as the progressive broadening of customer base and geographic market reach through digital channels, extending beyond conventional export-based measures of internationalization. Data were collected from 227 young women entrepreneurs operating small-scale food enterprises producing local agricultural and food specialties across Vietnam, and the proposed model was tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that digital transformation has a significant positive effect on both social commerce and market expansion performance, and that social commerce partially mediates the relationship between digital transformation and market expansion performance. Digital literacy significantly and positively moderates both the digital transformation–social commerce relationship and the social commerce–market expansion performance relationship, indicating that entrepreneurs’ digital competencies strengthen the conversion of digital capabilities into market-facing outcomes. These findings extend the application of the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory to digitally enabled market expansion in an emerging-market, gender-specific, and place-based entrepreneurial context. The study offers practical implications for young women entrepreneurs, provincial authorities, and national policymakers seeking to strengthen digital capabilities and social commerce practices to help geographically and culturally rooted local specialties reach broader domestic and international markets.

title: Authentic or strategic ESG? Motive attribution, consumer–company identification and purchase intention in retailing
summary: Against the backdrop of widespread greenwashing skepticism, consumers are increasingly scrutinizing corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) motives rather than simply accepting ESG disclosures at face value, creating a fundamental ethical dilemma in which ESG investment may fail to translate into market returns if corporate actions are attributed to strategic calculation rather than genuine values. Drawing on attribution theory and social identity theory, this study examines how Chinese retail consumers internalize ESG perceptions, through sincere versus strategic motive judgments, into consumer-company identification (CCI), and how this psychological process ultimately drives purchase intention, using a multi-study design in which Study 1 (N = 226) employed a cross-sectional survey of Chinese retail consumers to test the associative pathways and mediation effects among the key variables, while Study 2 (N = 156) employed a single-factor, two-level between-subjects experiment with structural equation modeling (SEM) and 5000-resample bootstrap estimation to examine the proposed direct and indirect effects. Three core findings emerge. First, corporate ESG performance exerts a robust positive effect on purchase intention even in skeptical environments. Second, CCI serves as the critical psychological bridge linking ESG performance to market response. Third, experimental causal evidence reveals that sincere motive attribution is the key trigger for activating CCI, with the indirect effect through identification accounting for 38.3% of the total effect, revealing a “dual-channel structure” in which a direct effect and an indirect, identification-mediated effect coexist. These findings offer actionable implications for ESG communication strategy in China's retail sector and provide a basis for future comparative research in other Asia-Pacific emerging markets.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Customs Compliance and Risk Management: Evidence Gaps and Research Priorities for Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: This systematic review examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in customs compliance and risk management, within Customs Administrations and how it can be tailored to Sub-Saharan Africa Customs Administrations. The study synthesizes 38 primary sources and identifies a transition from rule-based systems to predictive modelling, particularly for enhancing fraud detection and revenue optimization . Further, for SSA Customs Administrations, findings reveal a significant "revenue paradox" which demands an urgent need for adoption, however, infrastructure deficits and symbolic institutional adoption often hinder the realization of adoption and use of AI in customs compliance and risk management. The review also highlights critical evidence gaps regarding regional scalability and the psychological dimensions of stakeholder trust. The study emphasizes the necessity of localized frameworks to ensure sustainable digital transformation. The paper concludes with administrative recommendations for enhancing operational transparency and algorithmic sovereignty in emerging digital economies.

title: Strategic Alignment vs. Operational Reality: Analyzing Structural Friction Between International Corporate Governance Mandates and Performance Indicators (KPIs) in High-Velocity Global Industries
summary: Dominant theoretical models in corporate governance and management control systems assume that Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are linearly designed to maximize long-term economic value, optimize resource allocation, and foster rational organizational behavior. However, empirical evidence derived from managerial practice within large-scale corporations reveals a systematic and profound fracture between the strategic directives issued by global boards and the operational reality faced by local subsidiaries. This study explores and maps the structural pathologies and logical short-circuits generated by misaligned incentive frameworks that institutionalize a form of organizational schizophrenia, compelling management to navigate distorted ethical and operational trade-offs to satisfy formal numerical metrics.From a methodological standpoint, to ensure the highest standards of confidentiality, reputational protection, and absolute anonymity for all entities involved, the research adopts a qualitative approach anchored in the paradigms of Analytical Autoethnography and Aggregated Multi-Case Synthesis. The empirical dataset draws from the author’s direct participant observation and fieldwork, accumulated over a span of more than twenty-five years in managerial positions within multiple multinational corporations. Operational data and corporate occurrences have been entirely stripped of sectoral, chronological, and geographic coordinates, subsequently deconstructed and synthesized into four macro-archetypes of asynchronous corporate behavior: (1) Volume Hypertrophy at Negative Margins, (2) Dogmatic Compliance to Centralized Planning, (3) The Asymmetric Premium Positioning Illusion, and (4) Reverse Financial Engineering and Mix Coercion.In alignment with Goodhart’s Law, this study demonstrates how rigid quantification and the obsession with quarterly metrics drive boards to reward ritualistic efficiency while actively penalizing the logical and constructive dissent of rational managers. The paper bridges a critical gap in business ethics and general management literature, providing future chief executives and control committees with pragmatic guidelines to design flexible KPI architectures anchored to real-world market dynamics, thereby safeguarding the strategic, financial, and human integrity of the global enterprise.

title: Improving the methodology for conducting an internal audit of fixed assets of a machine-building enterprise
summary: In today’s economic conditions, one of the factors contributing to an organization’s sustainable development is improving the use of its assets. The fixed assets used by organizations serve as their most important economic resource, influencing the increase in capital productivity, the number of services provided, the reduction in their cost, and, most importantly, the growth of profits. Fixed assets (machinery, equipment, buildings, structures, etc.) form the basis of the production potential of machine-building enterprises. Their technical condition, level of automation, and degree of wear and tear directly determine the volume of output, quality, and cost. Modernization and renewal of fixed assets are key factors in increasing production efficiency. Given the complexity and variability of the regulatory framework, as well as the large range of items and the geographical dispersion of fixed assets within a single enterprise, there is a need to organize an internal audit in order to comply with legislation in the field of accounting, monitor fixed assets, and improve the efficiency of their use. Based on a comparative analysis of economic literature and an assessment of these regulatory documents, the article systematizes existing approaches to the interpretation of the concepts of «internal audit» and «fixed assets», identifies their key similarities and differences, provides a critical overview of existing methods of internal audit of fixed assets and suggests an author’s methodology that takes into account the specifics of the engineering industry. Particular attention is paid to contradictions in the criteria for recognition of fixed assets, including cost limits and purposes of use, which creates risks of distortion of financial statements. The authors propose refined definitions of the categories under study, synthesizing modern requirements of international standards and national regulations. The application of the developed approach makes it possible to unify the process of asset identification, minimize the subjectivity of assessments and improve the quality of internal audits and control over the fixed assets of a machine-building enterprise.

title: Determinants of Digital Marketing Adoption and MSME Performance in Indonesia’s Halal Food Sector
summary: Background Digital transformation has become a strategic pillar of Indonesia’s economy, with an estimated contribution of USD 130 billion by 2025. Halal Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), particularly in the food and beverage sector, contribute approximately USD 180 billion annually, account for around 60% of Indonesia’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and employ nearly 97% of the national workforce. However, digital marketing adoption among halal MSMEs remains limited due to low digital literacy, inadequate infrastructure, financial constraints, and inconsistent implementation of sharia business principles. This study examines the determinants of digital marketing adoption and its influence on the performance of halal MSMEs in Indonesia. Methods This study employed an explanatory quantitative research design based on the Technology–Organization–Environment–Personal (TOEP) framework. Data were collected from 500 halal-certified MSMEs operating in the food and beverage sector across Indonesia using a structured questionnaire. Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4.0 was used to evaluate the relationships among technological, organizational, environmental, and personal factors, digital marketing adoption, and business performance. Results The findings indicate that technological, organizational, environmental, and personal factors significantly influence digital marketing adoption among halal MSMEs. Furthermore, digital marketing adoption has a positive and significant effect on business performance by improving operational efficiency, increasing customer loyalty, strengthening halal brand visibility, and enhancing overall business competitiveness. Conclusions Digital marketing adoption is a key strategic driver for improving the competitiveness and sustainability of halal MSMEs in Indonesia. Strengthening digital capabilities through technological readiness, organizational support, favorable business environments, and personal competencies is essential to accelerate digital transformation and maximize the contribution of halal MSMEs to the national digital economy.

title: The impact of corporate governance on enhancing financial performance through risk management (An analytical study of the opinions of a sample of managers in some banks in the city of Sulaymaniyah / Kurdistan Region of Iraq)
summary: The digitization of human resource management has become a modern trend attracting increasing attention in contemporary organizations due to its active role in developing administrative practices and improving the efficiency of human resource utilization. The digitization of human resource management refers to the use of digital technologies and electronic systems to expedite procedures, reduce errors, and improve the quality of administrative services. Digital systems also help organize work and clearly distribute tasks, which positively impacts task performance and raises employee performance levels. Based on this, this research aims to investigate the role of the digitization of human resource management as an independent variable in improving job performance as a dependent variable, with its dimensions of: (task performance, contextual performance, and anti-productivity behaviors). Two main hypotheses were formulated, from which three sub-hypotheses branched out, to test the correlation and influence relationships between the research variables. The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach. The study population consisted of human resources working in the Duhok Governorate Traffic Directorate, totaling (1001) respondents, while the study sample comprised (129) respondents selected using random sampling. The research data was collected by distributing 150 questionnaires to human resources personnel working at the Duhok Governorate Traffic Directorate. 129 questionnaires were returned and deemed valid for statistical analysis. The results showed a statistically significant positive relationship between the digitization of human resources management and job performance. Furthermore, the results indicated a significant impact of digitized human resources management on job performance across its three dimensions. Based on these findings, the research suggests the necessity of sustainably investing in and promoting digitized applications in human resources management at the Duhok Governorate Traffic Directorate to support improved job performance among its employees. The research also suggests conducting future studies addressing other relevant variables.

title: Do female CEOs really promote investment efficiency?
summary: This study examines whether female CEOs moderate the relationship between accrual-based earnings management (EM) and corporate investment efficiency. Using panel data on 267 French firms listed on the CAC All Shares index over 2011–2022 (3,204 firm-year observations), we assess whether firms led by women exhibit different patterns of overinvestment and underinvestment. Our findings suggest that the positive association between accrual-based EM and overinvestment is weaker in female-CEO firms, consistent with capital discipline. However, the interaction between female CEOs and EM is positively associated with the magnitude of underinvestment among underinvesting firm-years, suggesting a more cautious investment pattern when reporting opacity is high. Our results also suggest that board diversity, reflected by gender diversity, cultural diversity and soft-skills heterogeneity, is associated with a weaker relationship between EM and investment inefficiency, suggesting a complementary governance role. This study underscores the governance (G) dimension of ESG and its implications for sustainable corporate investment policies.

title: Corporate strategy for the green transition: Are executive incentives effective?
summary: This paper examines whether green incentives embedded in executive compensation schemes are associated with a reorientation of firms' innovative activities toward environmentally sustainable technologies. Drawing on agency theory and the attention-based view of the firm, we conceptualize green incentives as governance and management-control devices that can mitigate managerial short-termism and channel executive attention toward long-horizon environmental objectives, thereby redirecting firms' technological search. Using a panel of publicly listed U.S. and European firms that participate in the Carbon Disclosure Project over the period 2010–2020, we analyse green innovation as a multi-stage process comprising the reorientation of technological search (the distance of firms' patent portfolios from green domains), knowledge recombination (the citation of green prior art in non-green patents), and realized green innovation output (green patent counts and shares). Firms adopting green incentives exhibit higher green innovation output, a significant repositioning of their knowledge portfolios toward green technological domains, and a greater integration of green knowledge into non-green technologies. These associations are weaker among firms experiencing a recent deterioration in carbon performance, and are strongest among continental European firms. Overall, the findings suggest that executive green incentives are associated with the direction, and not merely the volume, of firms' innovative activities, highlighting the role of internal governance mechanisms in sustainability transitions while recognising the limits of causal inference in observational data.

title: THE EFFECT OF ACCOUNTING KNOWLEDGE AND WORK MOTIVATION ON THE USE OF ACCOUNTING INFORMATION AT CV ASA TAX SOLUTION
summary: This study aims to determine the effect of accounting knowledge and work motivation partially on the use of accounting information at CV Asa Tax Solution. This research employed a quantitative approach. The population of this study consisted of employees of CV Asa Tax Solution, and the sampling technique used was saturated sampling. The research sample consisted of 30 respondents. The data were collected using a questionnaire, while data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS. The results indicate that accounting knowledge has a positive effect on the use of accounting information. This finding suggests that employees with higher accounting knowledge tend to make greater use of accounting information in carrying out their work activities. Work motivation also has a positive effect on the use of accounting information, indicating that motivated employees are morelikely to utilize accounting information in supporting their job performance. These findings demonstrate that accounting knowledge and work motivation are important factors influencing the use of accounting information at CV Asa Tax Solution.

title: Facilitating ambidextrous innovation through digitalisation? Evidence from Chinese A-share listed companies
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine whether digital transformation promotes exploratory and exploitative innovation as well as their balanced development, and to investigate the mechanisms through which digital transformation affects firms’ ambidextrous innovation. Design/methodology/approach Using firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2013 to 2022, this study empirically examines the effects of digital transformation on exploratory innovation, exploitative innovation and the balance between them, and further investigates the underlying mechanisms and heterogeneous effects. Findings Digital transformation significantly promotes both exploratory and exploitative innovation, but its effect is stronger on exploratory innovation, thereby widening the gap between the two innovation modes. Human capital structure, internal control costs and investment decision quality constitute important transmission mechanisms. The imbalance-aggravating effect is more pronounced among non-manufacturing and non-high-tech firms and in regions with weaker institutional environments. A more developed digital environment strengthens the positive effect of digital transformation on exploitative innovation. Originality/value This study moves beyond the conventional focus on whether digital transformation promotes innovation by adopting a balance-oriented perspective on organizational ambidexterity. It reveals the asymmetric effects of digital transformation on exploratory and exploitative innovation and identifies multiple internal mechanisms through which such imbalance emerges.

title: Tenure as a boundary condition of employee performance: A study of work stress, motivation, and compensation among hospital accounting and finance staff in Manado City
summary: Employee performance in hospital accounting and finance departments underpins the accuracy and timeliness of financial reporting, yet it is continually tested by tight closing deadlines, repeated claim verification, and heavy administrative workloads. This study examines the effects of work stress, work motivation, and compensation on the performance of accounting and finance employees at Type C hospitals in Manado City, Indonesia, and tests length of service (tenure) as a moderator of all three relationships. Grounded in Goal Setting Theory and Human Capital Theory, the study employs a quantitative survey design, drawing data from accounting and finance employees across Type C hospitals in Manado and analyzing it using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. The measurement model satisfied recommended validity and reliability thresholds. Work stress is found to negatively and significantly affect employee performance, whereas work motivation and compensation each have a positive and significant effect, jointly explaining a substantial share of the variance in performance. Contrary to the expectation that accumulated experience strengthens or weakens these relationships, tenure does not significantly moderate any of the three paths, a pattern attributed to limited statistical power rather than multicollinearity or a genuine absence of a moderating mechanism. Hospital management should therefore treat stress mitigation, motivational support, and fair compensation as direct and universal levers of performance rather than assuming that seniority buffers their effects. The study extends Goal Setting Theory and Human Capital Theory into hospital financial administration and clarifies the boundary conditions of tenure as a moderator.

title: IVPNSDWGA: An Enhanced Dombi-Based Interval-Valued Pythagorean Neutrosophic Aggregation Model for SDG-Driven Sustainable Investment Decision
summary: Decision-making in the area of sustainable and green finance often depends on information that is uncertain and difficult to express using conventional numerical methods.This issue becomes more apparent when evaluating environmental, social, and governance (ESG) indicators, as expert judgements in this context are typically imprecise and may overlap with one another.To address this limitation, the present study proposed a novel aggregation mechanism for Interval Valued Pythagorean Neutrosophic Sets (IVPNS), referred to as the Interval-Valued Pythagorean Neutrosophic Dombi Weighted Geometric Average (IVPNSDWGA) aggregation operator.The proposed aggregation operator incorporates Dombi t-norm and t-conorm functions into the IVPNS framework.It enables a more realistic representation of interval values based on linguistic information and the inherent uncertainty in expert evaluations.The mathematical properties of the operator, including idempotency, monotonicity, and boundedness, are examined to ensure its consistency and suitability in multi-attribute decision-making environments.The proposed operator is applied to demonstrate the practical applicability in the sustainable investment problem involving the evaluation of green-oriented companies.The case study evaluates the green sector and alignment with selected Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).The findings demonstrate that the proposed operator produces consistent, stable rankings even when the input data are imprecise.The IVPNSDWGA offers better alternative discrimination than current aggregation techniques, particularly when expert evaluations involve overlapping or uncertain information.These results indicate that the proposed operator offers a practical and reliable tool for sustainability-driven financial decisions, where uncertainty plays a central role.

title: From Green Spending to Green Priorities: A Sub-Thematic Analysis of Environmental CSR in Selected Maharatna Companies, 2014-15 to 2023-24
summary: Environmental sustainability is a recognised field of corporate social responsibility (CSR) under India's mandatory CSR framework, yet aggregate environmental expenditure reveals little about the specific ecological concerns companies prioritise. This study develops a controlled sub-thematic analysis of environmental CSR undertaken by Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC), NTPC Limited, Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), and Coal India Limited (CIL) during 2014-15 to 2023-24. Verified evidence was classified into six substantive sub-themes: afforestation and biodiversity; water conservation; waste and circular resources; clean energy; pollution control and natural-resource conservation; and environmental awareness and climate resilience. Non-disaggregated environmental expenditure was retained separately as G7 rather than estimated across themes. The classification audit corrected project assignments, excluded non-environmental records, and suppressed exact duplicate activity records. Monetary traceability differed sharply: 10.92% for ONGC, zero for NTPC and SAIL, and 90.93% for CIL. Consequently, expenditure-based sub-theme concentration is interpreted only where financial disaggregation permits it. A supplementary analysis of 442 unique specifically coded project/activity records shows clean energy dominating ONGC's identified activity orientation, afforestation and biodiversity dominating NTPC and SAIL, and waste-related activity being most frequent in CIL. Kendall's coefficient of concordance across the six activity-record rankings is 0.637 (p = .026), indicating significant but disclosure-sensitive commonality. The study concludes that environmental CSR analysis must distinguish financial commitment from reported activity orientation and that standardised project-level expenditure disclosure is necessary for reliable comparisons of corporate green priorities.

title: The Role of Green Logistics in Enhancing Sustainability in the Cement Industry: A Systematic Literature Review from a Saudi Arabian Perspective
summary: Objectives: This systematic literature review examines how green logistics can enhance environmental sustainability, operational efficiency, and economic performance in the cement industry, with particular attention to the Saudi Arabian context. The review focuses on sustainable transportation, logistics network optimization, digital logistics systems, and supply chain collaboration as key practices that may reduce logistics-related environmental impacts in cement supply chains. Methods: The study followed the PRISMA 2020 logic for identifying, screening, assessing, and synthesizing relevant studies. A structured search was conducted primarily through Google Scholar using Publish or Perish, supported by supplementary verification through academic indexing platforms and publisher databases where accessible. The search covered English-language peer-reviewed literature published between 2015 and 2026. After applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, 46 studies were retained. Data were extracted according to author, year, sector, country or region, methodology, type of contribution, and relevance to green logistics and sustainability. A simplified CASP/JBI-informed quality appraisal was also applied to assess the strength of the evidence. Results: The thematic synthesis identified four dominant themes. Sustainable transportation appeared in 34 studies (74%), logistics network optimization in 28 studies (61%), digital logistics systems in 21 studies (46%), and supply chain collaboration in 18 studies (39%). The findings suggest that green logistics contributes to sustainability by reducing freight-related emissions, improving route and distribution efficiency, enhancing supply chain visibility, and supporting coordinated environmental action across logistics partners. Conclusions: Green logistics represents a practical and policy-relevant approach for improving sustainability in the Saudi cement industry. However, the evidence also shows that implementation outcomes depend on sectoral conditions, infrastructure readiness, digital maturity, regulatory support, and supply chain coordination. The review highlights the need for more empirical Saudi cement-sector studies and for stronger integration between logistics policy, industrial decarbonization, and sustainability performance measurement.

title: ESG factors in the system of ensuring long-term financial security of organizations in the agro-industrial complex
summary: This article examines the impact of ESG (environmental, social, and governance) factors on the long-term financial security of organizations in the agro-industrial complex. It argues that the integration of ESG criteria is becoming a necessary condition for reducing cash flow volatility, the cost of borrowed capital, and strategic vulnerability. Using dairy farming as a case study, the authors propose an original system of threshold values for ESG indicators to diagnose levels of financial security (high, risk zone, critical). The study demonstrates that incorporating non-financial factors into default prediction models significantly improves their accuracy compared to traditional liquidity and financial stability ratios. The risks of greenwashing (imitation of sustainable practices) are identified, along with methodological limitations related to the heterogeneity of industry-specific approaches and regional characteristics. The article concludes that developing long-term roadmaps to reduce the carbon footprint and enhance governance transparency is essential for ensuring the genuine financial security of agricultural enterprises.

title: Reconciliation-Invariant Testing for Statutory Investment Accounting Engines
summary: Aim: This study aims to develop and demonstrate a reconciliation-invariant testing approach for detecting arithmetic, temporal, duplication, and reference-consistency defects in the ingestion and reconciliation layer of statutory investment accounting engines. Methods: The method was evaluated through a controlled demonstration using synthetic multi-entity investment statements comprising clean baseline records and six predefined defect classes, including OCR errors, roll-forward breaks, silent restatements, numerical precision errors, duplicate ingestion, and reference divergence. Results: The main invariants are that the ending value equals the beginning value plus the activity of the period‚ that the value equals the number of shares times the price‚ and that the opening value of the current period equals the last period’s ending value․ Additionally‚ there is a reference assertion‚ an idempotency assertion‚ a SHA-256 repository of each document source‚ and a continuity assertion‚ which also serves a purpose as a silent restatement detector․ Failed assertions are not written to the ledger‚ but are instead sent to a human for review․ Generation of schedules has not yet been implemented; however‚ this has been demonstrated on synthetic multi-entity statements with defects injected․ Each failed assertion stopped execution at the control while valid statements continued. Conclusion: The demonstration provides proof-of-concept evidence that the proposed controls can detect the predefined classes of arithmetic, continuity, duplication, and reference-consistency defects before ledger posting. Recommendation: Future work should extend the approach to statutory schedule generation and evaluate it using larger real-world datasets across multiple accounting systems.

title: Audit Committee Financial Expertise and Fraud Prevention: Evidence from Nigerian Listed Deposit Money Banks
summary: Audit committees are statutorily established in listed deposit money banks (DMBs), yet fraud cases continue to rise, raising concerns about whether the financial competence of audit committee members influences fraud prevention. The correlation between audit committee financial expertise level and fraud prevention in the DMBs listed in Nigeria was examined in this study. The study was based on agency theory, and took a correlational design with secondary data obtained from the annual reports of the 15 DMBs listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) and also from the fraud report of the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) for 2014-2023. A census approach was adopted; Premium Trust Bank Plc (which appeared in 2023, with one year of data only) and six bank-years with irreconcilable missing data were excluded leaving a sample of 135 firm-year observations from 14 banks. Fraud prevention was measured by a composite fraud prevention index (fraud amount ratio, fraud frequency, and disclosure score) that reflects the inverse of fraud incidence, and audit committee financial expertise was defined by the percentage of members with recognised accounting or finance qualifications. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and random-effects panel regression (as determined by the Hausman specification test) in STATA 17. The financial expertise of the audit committee had a positive association and also was significant to fraud prevention (β = 0.3245, z = 3.70, p < 0.01). Meeting frequency (β = 0.0876, p < 0.01) and female membership (β = 0.2345, p < 0.05) were also positively and significantly correlated with fraud prevention, with independence having no significant correlation. The study finds that audit committee competence is an important correlate of fraud prevention in the Nigerian DMBs. The study recommends that the Central Bank of Nigeria should require at least 2 members of the audit committee in every bank to be financially competent and that banks should seek to appoint professionally qualified accountants to enhance fraud control.

title: Do ESG Performance and Carbon Taxes Mitigate Climate Change? Evidence from Carbon Tax-Adopting Countries
summary: Abstract: Climate change is a pressing global issue, necessitating effective policy interventions and sustainable corporate practices. This study examines the impact of ESG scores, carbon taxation, and carbon emissions on temperature change in countries that have implemented carbon tax policies. Using panel data from 2000 to 2020, the study seeks to evaluate the effectiveness of both corporate sustainability initiatives and environmental fiscal policies in addressing climate change. The findings indicate that higher ESG performance and effective carbon tax mechanisms are significantly associated with reduced temperature change, indicating their potential role in mitigating environmental degradation and supporting climate goals. Conversely, increased carbon emissions are found to contribute positively to temperature change, highlighting their adverse environmental consequences. These results suggest that a combination of strong sustainability practices and well-designed carbon pricing policies can play a crucial role in reducing the environmental impact of economic activities. title: Bibliometric analysis of green entrepreneurship as a driver of sustainable innovation in Saudi Arabia
summary: This study examines the role of green entrepreneurship in fostering sustainable innovation and supporting the growth of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Saudi Arabia, a priority reinforced by the Vision 2030 transformation agenda. Despite increasing policy and academic attention, there remains a lack of a comprehensive and context-specific synthesis of the rapidly expanding literature on green entrepreneurship in Saudi Arabia. The accelerating implementation of Vision 2030, coupled with growing interest in digital transformation, green finance, and sustainable innovation, makes an updated review particularly timely. Unlike previous reviews that have examined green entrepreneurship from a broader international perspective, this study provides the first Saudi Arabia-focused systematic review and bibliometric analysis that integrates economic, technological, institutional, and socio-cultural determinants—including Vision 2030 reforms, Islamic environmental ethics, artificial intelligence-enabled innovation, and SME development—within a unified analytical framework. This research addresses this gap through a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of 249 Scopus-indexed publications (2016–2024), conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and supported by R and VOSviewer software to map publication trends, influential contributors and thematic evolution. The findings reveal a strong increase in research activity, with sustainable innovation primarily driven by circular economy capabilities, human resource management practices and the adoption of artificial intelligence and digital tools. However, growth remains constrained by financial barriers, regulatory complexity and uneven technological readiness among SMEs. This study offers an integrated and context-specific synthesis of how green entrepreneurship supports sustainable innovation in Saudi Arabia and provides theoretical and policy-oriented insights to strengthen a resilient and innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem.
